androidFlow: Android uses a dial-centric in-place tab model. The compact bottom bar (ChronosCompactFloatingBottomBar) displays only 3 shell destination tabs: Plan, Today, Focus (plus Quick-Add FAB). These three are IN-PLACE tabs that don't change the back stack - they surface different targets (Day.TARGET_PLAN, Day.TARGET_TODAY, Day.TARGET_FOCUS_PLANNER) inside DayDialScreen via selectDayTarget(). Secondary destinations (Tasks, Habits, Goals, Medication, Review) are NOT bottom-bar tabs; they're reached via Quick-Add FAB menu, command palette, or on tablets a navigation rail. The FAB (ChronosQuickAddButton + ChronosQuickAddMenu) expands into action buttons (New block/task/med/habit/goal/Journal/Sleep) plus a natural-language typed quick-capture field. On tablets, the navigation rail (ChronosAdaptiveNavigationRail) shows all destinations as a sidebar. Back navigation is hierarchical: sub-sections (Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds) push on top of Day, and system back exits them.
iosFlow: iOS uses a flat TabView(.sidebarAdaptable) listing every screen as a top-level tab: Plan, Today, Focus, Tasks, Track (a TabSection grouping Habits, Goals, Meds, Routines, Sleep, Journal), Review, Settings. The floating QuickAddButton (56x56 FAB) overlays the tab bar bottom-trailing, and tapping it presents QuickAddSheet (a NavigationStack with a List showing the same action buttons as Android plus typed input). There is no command palette. On iPad, .sidebarAdaptable converts the tabs into a sidebar, but the structure remains flat - all screens are sibling top-level destinations, not in-place tabs. Back navigation is per-screen; there's no cross-screen hierarchical back stack like Android.

divergences.description: Bottom bar has 3 primary tabs (Plan/Today/Focus) that stay in-place with sub-targets, vs iOS flat 12+ tabs. Android's secondary destinations (Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds/Review) are NOT bottom-bar tabs; iOS lists them as top-level tabs alongside primaries.
divergences.androidBehavior: Plan, Today, Focus are physical tabs that route to Day(target=Plan/Today/Focus) in-place inside DayDialScreen; no back stack change. selectDayTarget() updates requestedDayTarget and dayTargetGeneration without navigating. Secondary destinations exist as shell destinations but showInCompact=false, so they never appear in the 3-tab pill.
divergences.iosBehavior: All 12 destinations (Plan, Today, Focus, Tasks, Habits, Goals, Meds, Routines, Sleep, Journal, Review, Settings) are equally-weighted top-level tabs in TabView. Switching between any two tabs is equivalent; there's no 'in-place' concept.
divergences.fix: Restructure RootView.swift to have only Plan, Today, Focus as primary tabs in the TabView, keeping all other screens reachable ONLY via the Quick-Add FAB menu (tapping them closes the FAB and shows an inline editor in the current tab context) or via command palette. Alternatively, keep secondary destinations accessible but hidden from the tab bar by making them non-tab sheets/modals triggered from the FAB or by navigation within a tab.

divergences.description: Quick-Add is a FAB that expands a menu with action buttons + typed input (Android) vs iOS sheet that lists actions without in-line menu expansion.
divergences.androidBehavior: ChronosQuickAddButton is a 56dp FAB with a rotating +. Tapping it sets quickAddExpanded=true, which reveals ChronosQuickAddMenu below it (animated scale + fade). Menu shows all quickAddActionsFor(featureFlags) (6-7 buttons) and a ChronosQuickCaptureInput field. Tapping an action routes navState.navigate(action.route) and closes the menu. Typing text triggers onQuickCapturePreview (runs previewQuickCaptureCommand) for live-preview label.
divergences.iosBehavior: QuickAddButton is a 56x56 circle with a + image, positioned absolute bottom-trailing. Tapping it presents QuickAddSheet, a NavigationStack with List sections (typed input + Create buttons). Selecting an action sets editor state, which then presents the appropriate editor sheet. Typed input parses with parseSmartFill locally; no live preview is shown, only a helper label below the input.
divergences.fix: Change QuickAddSheet to use a ZStack with the same animated expansion/collapse as Android: toggle an isExpanded state on the button, and conditionally show the menu above it with scale+fade animation. Implement the live-preview callback (onQuickCapturePreview) same as Android — parse input, return a label like 'Add task "..."', show it in the footer. Route selections directly via navigation instead of setting an editor state.

divergences.description: Android has a command palette (Ctrl+K) accessible from anywhere. iOS has no command palette.
divergences.androidBehavior: Ctrl+K opens CommandPaletteDialog (MainActivity.kt). It lists quickCreateCommandProvider (New block/task/med/habit/goal/journal/sleep), dayDialCommandProvider (Today/Plan/Focus/Review/tools), focusCommandProvider, taskCommandProvider, habitCommandProvider, goalCommandProvider, medicationCommandProvider. User can type to filter. Selecting an item executes its command (navigate to a route or run a function). There's also an Ask Assistant option.
divergences.iosBehavior: No equivalent. All creation and navigation is via tabs or the Quick-Add sheet.
divergences.fix: Add a CommandPaletteView to iOS (similar to Android's CommandPaletteDialog). Trigger it with a keyboard shortcut (Cmd+K on iPhone, likely a Menu button on iPad) or a dedicated toolbar button. Populate it with the same command providers. Implement a simple filter/search UI that matches the Android version. Call the same command callbacks (navigate to screens, open sheets, etc.).

divergences.description: Android: Double-tap Today tab resets the dial to today's date (TARGET_TODAY_RESET). iOS: TodayView has no equivalent reset behavior.
divergences.androidBehavior: onShellDestinationDoubleClick checks if destination.id == SHELL_TODAY and calls navState.selectDayTarget(ChronosRoute.Day.TARGET_TODAY_RESET). DayDialScreen applies this target by snapping selectedDate back to today.
divergences.iosBehavior: TodayView is always today; there's no date picker like Plan. Double-tapping the Today tab doesn't reset anything because TodayView is not a date-picker screen.
divergences.fix: Add a double-tap gesture to the Today tab indicator. On double-tap, ensure the selected date in the active day view (if the user had browsed to another day in Plan) resets to today. Alternatively, add a 'Jump to today' button in TodayView if it ever shows an off-today state.

divergences.description: Bottom-bar selection indicator: Android has a single animated sliding pill (iOS-style) that glides between tab items. iOS uses the native TabView indicator, which varies by iOS version and style.
divergences.androidBehavior: ChronosCompactFloatingBottomBar draws a single RoundRect (indicatorColor = primaryContainer) that animates its x position and width as the user taps tabs. The pill is drawn in drawBehind; both x and width animate with ChronosValueAnimationFactory.navIndicator(reducedMotion).
divergences.iosBehavior: TabView(.sidebarAdaptable) uses the native iOS tab-bar styling (underline or background highlight that varies by OS). No custom sliding pill.
divergences.fix: Implement a custom TabView-like container with the same animated sliding pill as Android. Use Canvas or custom layout + animateAsState to track the selected tab's frame and draw the pill. This is a visual refinement; the core functionality works with native TabView but doesn't match Android's aesthetic.

divergences.description: Android: Back stack is hierarchical (Day at root, sub-sections push on top). iOS: All tabs are siblings; no hierarchical back.
divergences.androidBehavior: ChronosNavigationState.backStack is flattened: Day always anchors it, and at most one sub-section sits on top. goBack() exits the sub-section and returns to Day. On-screen back handlers route back through the sub-section's NavDisplay first, then to the system back event.
divergences.iosBehavior: Each tab is a NavigationStack, but tab-switching doesn't interact with back stacks. Pressing back within a tab (iPad sidebar back button or swipe) navigates within that tab's stack. Switching to another tab is independent.
divergences.fix: Model the back stack as Android does: track the current section and sub-section in a state holder (similar to ChronosNavigationState). When the user taps a secondary destination (Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds/Review) in the Quick-Add menu or command palette, push it onto a back stack and show it as an overlay or as the active screen, with a back button returning to the Day section. OR keep tabs flat but add a global back handler that routes back through the command palette or Quick-Add history.

divergences.description: Android: Adaptive layout shows a navigation rail on tablets (ChronosAdaptiveNavigationRail). iOS: .sidebarAdaptable flattens to a sidebar but structure is identical (all tabs become sidebar items).
divergences.androidBehavior: rememberChronosShellLayout() returns ADAPTIVE on tablets (WindowSizeClass.WIDTH_DP_MEDIUM_LOWER_BOUND). If showNavigationChrome=true, a vertical ChronosAdaptiveNavigationRail appears on the left with all expandedShellDestinations(featureFlags). The rail has a 'Navigate' header, each destination as a NavigationRailItem with icon+label+badge.
divergences.iosBehavior: .sidebarAdaptable automatically switches to a sidebar on iPad. The sidebar is just the flattened list of tabs (Plan, Today, Focus, Tasks, Track → Habits/Goals/..., Review, Settings), each with its own icon. No 'Navigate' header or badge support (badges don't appear in the sidebar naturally).
divergences.fix: Implement a custom adaptive layout that shows a sidebar on iPad but preserves the 3-primary / many-secondary structure: sidebar shows Plan/Today/Focus as primary items, and then a 'Track' section or 'Destinations' section listing Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds/Review. Implement badge support (show badge count next to each destination). Ensure tapping a secondary destination in the sidebar routes it correctly (either as a new top-level view or as an overlay).

divergences.description: Android: Shell destinations and Day tabs are aware of feature flags (showInCompact, isAvailable). iOS: Feature flags gate which tabs appear, but the logic is scattered in RootView.
divergences.androidBehavior: ChronosRoute.compactShellDestinations(featureFlags) filters by showInCompact && isAvailable(featureFlags). ChronosRoute.expandedShellDestinations(featureFlags) filters by isAvailable(featureFlags). Each ShellDestination checks its featureFlags at render time and appears/disappears as flags change.
divergences.iosBehavior: RootView uses if settings.habitsEnabled { Tab(...) } etc. The logic is inline in the TabView body, duplicated for each conditional feature.
divergences.fix: Extract the feature-flag logic into a structure like Android's ShellDestination (a computed property that returns only enabled destinations). Pass this to the tab builder so future feature additions only need to be added once.

divergences.description: Android: Deep links are routed via ChronosRoute.routeForNotificationLaunch(). iOS: Deep links use handleDeepLink(url) which maps URL hosts to tab selections.
divergences.androidBehavior: parseNotificationLaunch(intent) returns a NotificationLaunch. MainActivity.ChronosFlowApp checks featureFlags before navigating, routing disabled features back to Day(). RootView never shows disabled-feature screens.
divergences.iosBehavior: handleDeepLink(url) is a simple switch on url.host(), mapping 'today' → selection=.today, etc. It doesn't check feature flags; a link to a disabled feature will just switch to that tab and show a blank screen.
divergences.fix: Modify handleDeepLink() to check featureFlags and route disabled features back to Today. OR prevent disabled features from appearing in deep links by filtering them at the point of link generation (e.g., widgets, shortcuts).

divergences.description: Android: In-place sheets (Add block, Journal, Log sleep) open via Day targets (TARGET_ADD_BLOCK, TARGET_JOURNAL, TARGET_SLEEP), not as separate nav destinations. iOS: These are part of the create flow via Quick-Add, but not modeled as Day targets.
divergences.androidBehavior: daySheetLaunchTargets = {TARGET_ADD_BLOCK, TARGET_JOURNAL, TARGET_SLEEP}. selectDayTarget(target) sets requestedDayTarget, and dayLaunchTargetForRoute() applies the target, opening the sheet inside DayDialScreen. The sheet is in-place (doesn't change the back stack or the active destination).
divergences.iosBehavior: Quick-Add sheet has an editor state (case .block, .task, .sleep). Selecting one of these actions sets editor state, which then presents the editor sheet. There's no tie to Day targets; it's just the Quick-Add flow.
divergences.fix: Model in-place Day sheets as routes within Quick-Add (or add a dedicated 'openInPlace' callback that DayDialScreen can listen to). When the user selects 'New block' from the Quick-Add menu, instead of pushing a new sheet, pass a Day target callback that tells DayDialScreen to open the block editor overlay.

divergences.description: Android: Shell badges show on navigation items (Today shows missed-block count or off-today date; Review shows unread-insights count; Focus shows active indicator). iOS: No badges on tabs.
divergences.androidBehavior: badgeValueFor(destinationId, shellState, dayDialViewedDate) returns a string or null. ChronosCompactNavigationItem and ChronosAdaptiveNavigationRail both render BadgedBox with ChronosAnimatedBadge. Badges animate in/out with scale+fade.
divergences.iosBehavior: TabView doesn't natively support badges. The tabs have no visual indicator of missed blocks, unread insights, or active focus.
divergences.fix: Add badge support to the custom tab bar or sidebar: show a small red badge with a number (e.g., '3') next to Today if there are missed blocks, next to Review if there are unread insights, and a filled circle next to Focus if active. Use Shell-state data (ChronosShellState / ChronosShellViewModel equivalent) to drive the badge values.

area: DayDial central screen (dial canvas + Plan/Today/Focus/Insights tabs + top bar)
androidFlow:
Android uses a DIAL-CENTRIC single-screen architecture (DayDialScreen.kt, DayDialScreenChrome.kt, DayDialMainContent.kt):
- Single DayDialScreen composable houses ALL 4 primary tabs: Plan, Today, Focus, Insights
- These tabs are IN-PLACE (co-locate on one screen with a shared dial, date scrubber, top bar)
- DayDialTab enum defines the 4 primary tabs with shared context (sortedBlocks, date selection, etc.)
- Compact bottom bar shows only 3 tabs: Plan, Today, Focus (with Insights accessible via top-bar Review button or end-of-day sheet)
- Sidebar menu (floating pill) provides quick access to secondary pages (Tasks, Habits, Goals, Meds, Settings) which open as in-app sidebar pages, NOT separate destinations
- Date navigation via top bar date picker (DayDialTopBar.kt) affects ALL tabs' data simultaneously
- A single QuickAdd FAB expands to menu (New block/task/med/habit/goal, Journal, Sleep, command palette)
- All tab content (TodayTab, PlanTab, FocusTab, InsightsTab) shares: blocks, date state, focus session, undo/redo, snackbar host
- AnimatedContent transitions between tabs horizontally with predictable back to Today
iosFlow:
iOS uses a FLAT TabView architecture (RootView.swift):
- 12+ separate top-level Tab destinations in a TabView(.sidebarAdaptable): Plan, Today, Focus, Tasks, Habits, Goals, Meds, Routines, Sleep, Journal, Review (Insights), Settings
- Plan tab = DayDialScreen.swift (dial + conflict banner + free windows + block list)
- Today tab = TodayView.swift (separate view with "NOW" card, "NEXT" card, tasks, habits)
- Focus tab = FocusView.swift (separate view with timer ring + phase controls)
- Review tab = InsightsView.swift (separate view with period rollups + trends + recommendations)
- Each tab is independently routed and maintains its own @State; no shared date picker across tabs
- Date is hardcoded to TODAY in DayDialScreen.swift (selectedDate = Calendar.current.startOfDay(for: .now)) — no date navigation
- No shared dial across tabs; Today has its own "NOW" card, Focus has its own timer ring
- Quick-Add is a separate floating button (QuickAddButton) in RootView, presents QuickAddSheet
- Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds/Routines are full-screen separate tabs, not in-app sidebar pages
- Back gesture behavior differs: iOS tabs are independent; Android tabs fallback to Today

divergences.description: Android groups 4 primary tabs (Plan/Today/Focus/Insights) inside one DayDialScreen with in-place tab switching and shared state. iOS spreads them across separate TabView destinations, each with independent state and no shared dial.
divergences.androidBehavior: DayDialScreen.kt composes DayDialScreenChrome → DayDialMainContent → AnimatedContent over DayDialTab enum with TodayTab, PlanTab, FocusTab, InsightsTab all in-place. Tabs share sortedBlocks, selectedDate, focus session, undo/redo, snackbar. Switching tabs updates uiState.currentTab; back from non-Today tabs returns to Today.
divergences.iosBehavior: RootView.swift uses TabView(selection: $selection) with separate Tab { DayDialScreen() }, Tab { TodayView() }, Tab { FocusView() }, Tab { InsightsView() }. Each is a standalone NavigationStack. Date is hardcoded in each; no shared scrubber. Back gestures are independent per tab.
divergences.fix: Restructure iOS to match Android: (1) Create a single DayDialUnifiedScreen.swift that wraps all 4 tabs (Plan/Today/Focus/Insights) in one TabView or custom TabBar. (2) Extract shared state (selectedDate, sortedBlocks, focusSession, undo/redo) into a @Observable ViewModel. (3) Move date picker from individual views to the top bar. (4) Make back fallback to Today from Plan/Focus/Insights. (5) For iPad, promote the 3 primary tabs to main sidebar, secondary pages (Tasks/Habits etc) to a submenu/section. (6) Remove individual TodayView, FocusView, InsightsView; composite them as tabs inside DayDialUnifiedScreen.

divergences.description: Android's bottom bar is compact (3 tabs) with overflow handled by sidebar menu for Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds. iOS's TabView lists all 12+ as flat siblings (Tasks, Habits, Goals, Meds grouped under 'Track', plus Review, Settings). Missing in iOS: in-app sidebar pages, collapsible navigation, feature-gated tab filtering.
divergences.androidBehavior: Bottom nav shows Plan, Today, Focus only (DayDialTab.primary). Sidebar menu (DayDialSidebar.kt) is a floating pill opened by menu button; it lists Day-Tools, Tasks, Habits, Goals, Meds, Templates, Settings, Appearance, Notifications, Sync, etc. Tapping a menu item either opens an in-app sidebar page (e.g. TASKS → SidebarPage.TASKS) or routes to a full screen (e.g. TASKS → onOpenTasks()). Feature flags (habitsFeatureEnabled, etc.) determine which pages appear.
divergences.iosBehavior: TabView lists every screen as a peer tab. Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds are separate Tab destinations, not menu items. No sidebar menu. All tabs are always present (or filtered by feature flags post-hoc). No in-app sidebar pages.
divergences.fix: Reorganize iOS tabs to match Android's primary/secondary split: (1) Main tier: Plan, Today, Focus (+ break them out of their separate TabView destinations). (2) 'Track' section (TabSection in iOS 18+): Habits, Goals, Meds, Routines, Sleep, Journal (collapsed/subcollection on iPhone compact, sidebar on iPad). (3) Review and Settings as trailing items. (4) Implement a floating sidebar menu (or sheet) for secondary pages (Tasks, Habits as in-app pages, not full tabs) mirroring Android's SidebarPage enum. (5) Gate tabs by feature flags at the shell level, not downstream. (6) Convert in-app sidebar pages (Habits, Tasks entry points) to reusable components so they can appear both as tabs and as in-app pages.

divergences.description: Android's Today tab has rich live data (current block, next block, quick items for tasks/habits/meds, sleep readiness banner, quick actions to Plan/Focus). iOS's TodayView has some (NOW/NEXT cards, habits summary, quick actions) but no live dial, no undo/redo (only on Plan tab), no shared focus session state across tabs.
divergences.androidBehavior: TodayTab (DayDialMainContent.kt line 379) receives: activeBlock, nextBlock, missedBlocks, quickItems (tasks/habits/meds), sleepTrack, journalEntry, focusSession, focusRemainingSeconds, currentMinute. It renders a dial (ChronosDial) + active/next blocks + quick items (onQuickTaskDone, onQuickHabitDone, onQuickMedicationTaken). Links to Plan/Focus via callbacks (onOpenPlanTab, onOpenFocusScreen). Undo/redo available in top bar.
divergences.iosBehavior: TodayView.swift queries blocks/tasks/habits independently, renders NOW/NEXT cards, habit summary, quick action buttons (new task, new block, mood check-in, log sleep). No dial. No access to focusSession or focus timer. Undo/redo only appear in DayDialScreen (Plan tab). Quick actions pop sheets, not navigate to full tabs.
divergences.fix: (1) Promote focusSession state from DayDialViewModel to the unified screen's ViewModel so all tabs can read/write it. (2) Surface activeBlock and nextBlock in TodayView, not hardcoded to today. (3) Add a mini dial to TodayView (or share ChronosDialCanvas from Plan tab). (4) Surface quick items (tasks/habits/meds) across all tabs, not just Today. (5) Add undo/redo buttons to top bar in all tabs, not just Plan. (6) Route quick actions (new task, new block) to full tabs (Tasks, Plan) instead of inline sheets where appropriate.

divergences.description: Android dial (ChronosDial.kt) is the central visual element, shared across all 4 tabs. Today shows the dial with current/next block overlays. Plan shows blocks + suggested AI blocks. Focus shows a focus ring timer. Insights shows an empty dial. iOS Today has custom NOW/NEXT cards, Plan has its own dial (ChronosDialCanvas.swift), Focus has its own timer ring. No visual consistency across tabs.
divergences.androidBehavior: DayDialMainContent.kt composes DayDialPrimaryTabLayer for each tab, rendering a shared transition (AnimatedContent). All tabs receive the same sortedBlocks, currentMinute, selectedDate. The dial (ChronosDial) is only composed in TodayTab and PlanTab; FocusTab and InsightsTab have different visual hierarchies but the same layout/padding/top bar structure.
divergences.iosBehavior: DayDialScreen has ChronosDialCanvas (custom dial rendering, block dragging, conflict overlay). TodayView has custom VStack layout (NOW card, NEXT card, task list, habit summary), no dial. FocusView has a custom timerRing (Circle with progress stroke). InsightsView has period cards, charts, no dial.
divergences.fix: (1) Extract ChronosDialCanvas into a reusable component visible in Plan, Today, and optionally Focus tabs. (2) Share the same dial data (blocks, conflicts, free windows) across tabs via the unified ViewModel. (3) Add a compact dial or block timeline to TodayView. (4) Standardize the top bar (date picker, undo/redo, menu button) across all tabs. (5) Use the same AnimatedContent transition pattern for tab switching. (6) Compose each tab's content inside a consistent frame/padding/scroll structure.

divergences.description: Android date picker (top bar, DayDialTopBar.kt) affects all 4 tabs simultaneously and syncs with the single selectedDate state. iOS date picker only appears in DayDialScreen (Plan tab); Today is hardcoded to today; Focus has no date picker; Insights has no date picker.
divergences.androidBehavior: DayDialTopBar composes a date picker that calls viewModel.selectDate(). This updates vmState.selectedDate, which flows to ALL 4 tabs (TodayTab, PlanTab, FocusTab, InsightsTab) at once. Blocks, free windows, journal entry, sleep track, etc. all re-derive from the selected date.
divergences.iosBehavior: DayDialScreen has a DatePicker in toolbar (selection: $selectedDate). TodayView has no date picker (hardcoded to Calendar.current.startOfDay(for: .now)). FocusView and InsightsView have no date picker.
divergences.fix: (1) Move the date picker to the top bar of the unified screen so it's visible in all 4 tabs. (2) Bind the date picker to the unified ViewModel's selectedDate, not local @State. (3) In TodayView, subscribe to the ViewModel's selectedDate and re-fetch today's data (or default to .now if the selected date == today). (4) Add a date picker to InsightsView's toolbar to allow period drilling. (5) Mirror Android's date navigation flow: one picker, one state, all tabs update.

divergences.description: Android focus session state (focusSession: FocusSession?, focusRemainingSeconds, focusElapsedSeconds, focusSession.blockId) is held in the DayDialViewModel and accessible from all 4 tabs. iOS FocusView has a separate FocusTimerModel.shared singleton; other tabs (Today, Plan, Insights) have no reference to active focus session.
divergences.androidBehavior: DayDialScreen receives focusSession from the ViewModel. FocusTab renders a focus ring and phase controls, updating focusSession via viewModel callbacks (onStart, onPause, onResume, onFinish, etc.). TodayTab's nextBlock can show a 'Start focus' button. PlanTab can show focus-locked blocks. All tabs can see the active session.
divergences.iosBehavior: FocusView uses FocusTimerModel.shared (a singleton @Observable). TodayView and PlanTab have no reference to the active focus session. If focus is running on the Focus tab, switching to Today doesn't show the session state. No 'Start focus' button in Today.
divergences.fix: (1) Move FocusTimerModel state into the unified ViewModel (not a singleton). (2) Expose focusSession, focusRemainingSeconds, focusElapsedSeconds as @Published properties. (3) Pass these to all 4 tab components (TodayTab, PlanTab, FocusTab, InsightsTab). (4) Update TodayView to show a 'Start/Resume focus' action for the current block if a session is active. (5) Update PlanTab to highlight focus-protected blocks differently if a session is running. (6) Keep the FocusTimerModel for internal timer logic, but expose its state via the unified ViewModel.

divergences.description: Android has a unified undo/redo stack (PlannerCommandHistory in the ViewModel) shared by all 4 tabs. iOS undo/redo only works in DayDialScreen (Plan tab); other tabs have no undo/redo.
divergences.androidBehavior: vmState.canUndo and vmState.canRedo are derived from the ViewModel's undo/redo stack. Top bar shows undo/redo buttons when actionable. All 4 tabs contribute to the same stack: Plan tab can undo block moves, Today tab can undo quick-item completions, Focus tab can undo session ends, etc.
divergences.iosBehavior: DayDialScreen.swift has a local @State private var history = PlannerCommandHistory(). TodayView, FocusView, InsightsView have no undo/redo. Undo/redo buttons only appear in DayDialScreen's toolbar.
divergences.fix: (1) Move the PlannerCommandHistory into the unified ViewModel. (2) Expose canUndo/canRedo as @Published properties. (3) Add undo/redo toolbar buttons to the unified top bar (visible in all tabs). (4) Clear the history when selectedDate changes. (5) Wire up undo/redo callbacks from all tabs (Today's quick-item actions, Focus's session edits, etc.) to push commands onto the shared stack.

divergences.description: Android's Quick-Add FAB and command palette are global (feature/daydial/DayDialCommandProvider.kt). The FAB expands to: New block/task/med/habit/goal, Journal entry, Log sleep, typed quick-capture command. iOS Quick-Add is also global (RootView) but only covers: New task, New time block, Log sleep, Mood check-in.
divergences.androidBehavior: DayDialScreen receives onOpenCommandPalette callback. The FAB expands (SidebarMenu animation) to a menu with 8+ items. Selecting an item either opens a sheet (New block → SheetTarget.NewBlock(title)) or routes to a full screen (New task → onOpenTasks()). Some items (journal, sleep) trigger launch targets (applyLaunchTarget → SheetTarget.Journal, SheetTarget.SleepLog).
divergences.iosBehavior: QuickAddButton in RootView is a simple '+' button. Tapping it shows QuickAddSheet (Menu: New task, New time block, Log sleep, Mood check-in, + AI planning). Each action is a button that sets a local @State or routes via NavigationLink.
divergences.fix: (1) Expand iOS Quick-Add menu to include: New habit, New goal, New medication, Journal entry (if enabled), Sleep log (if enabled), typed quick-capture command. (2) Wire menu items to the same sheet/route handlers as Android (open Tasks full screen for new task, open DayDial for new block on today's date). (3) Add a command palette (text input + search) for quick commands (e.g. 'add 1h focus' parses to a block creation). (4) Gate menu items by feature flags (habitsEnabled, journalEnabled, etc.).

divergences.description: Android distinguishes between sidebar pages (in-app, navigated within Day) and full screens (Tasks, Habits, Goals, Meds). iOS conflates them: Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds are full-screen tabs. This breaks the Android mental model where secondary pages are closable/dismissible sheets/slides, not separate destinations.
divergences.androidBehavior: SidebarPage enum (SidebarPage.TASKS, SidebarPage.HABITS, etc.) defines pages opened from the Day screen's sidebar menu. They are composed inside SidebarPageContent (Feature/daydial/ui/SidebarPageContent.kt) and backed by live data (viewModel.routines, etc.). Tapping a Tasks item while on the sidebar page routes to the full Tasks screen (onOpenTasks()). The sidebar page is dismissible via back gesture; the full screen is not.
divergences.iosBehavior: RootView's TabView lists Tasks, Habits, Goals, Meds as peer tabs (not subordinate pages). No distinction between in-app pages and full screens.
divergences.fix: (1) On iPad: move Tasks/Habits/Goals/Meds from main sidebar to a submenu/TabSection. Make them open as in-app sidebar pages (not separate tabs) when selected from the primary Day menu. (2) On iPhone: implement a NavigationSplitView or custom modal slide for secondary pages so they feel like overlays, not separate destinations. (3) Implement the SidebarPage pattern: render in-app pages inside the Day screen's content area, not as top-level tabs. (4) Add a dismiss/back button to in-app pages so users can return to the dial without leaving the Day section.

area: Quick-Add menu, command palette & quick-capture (typed natural-language parsing into task/med/habit/goal)
androidFlow: Android shell (ChronosNavigationShell.kt) floats a FAB above bottom bar. Tapping it expands ChronosQuickAddMenu showing: (1) quickAddActionsFor() menu items (New block/task/meds/habits/goals, Journal, Log sleep) gated by feature flags; (2) ChronosQuickCaptureInput—a text field accepting natural language parsed by quickCaptureCreateCommands() (via CaptureIntentClassifier), which intelligently routes "call mom tomorrow" → task with detected action/date, "take vitamin d daily" → med with dose/frequency, etc. Preview shows "Ready to add [entity type] [parsed details]". Submission calls onQuickCaptureCommand. divergences.iosBehavior: Menu { ForEach(ChronosTextOp.allCases) { Button { rewriteNotes(op) } } }.
divergences.fix: Ensure iOS rewrite UI is styled and positioned similarly to Android. If iOS uses a menu, verify all rewrite styles are available and the UI is discoverable.

divergences.description: Android TaskScreen includes a TaskContextCommandSheet (lines 555-562, 899-977) that displays quick actions available for a task (call, email, link, map, app, files, schedule, edit, complete). iOS has no equivalent quick-action sheet.
divergences.androidBehavior: Bottom sheet shows task title, count of quick actions, a primary command (emphasized), and remaining options. Tapping a command fires the action (internal or external).
divergences.iosBehavior: No context command sheet; task actions are not visible or accessible from the task list.
divergences.fix: Port Android's TaskContextCommandSheet to iOS. Display as a BottomSheetModifier or ConfirmationDialog. Show primary action emphasized and remaining actions listed. Support internal actions (Schedule, Edit, Complete) and external actions (Call, Email, Link, Map, etc.).

divergences.description: Android TaskScreen automatically requests AI assist on context capture (lines 799-828); iOS has no auto-assist on task entry.
divergences.androidBehavior: LaunchedEffect monitors taskTitle/description/taskCaptureContext and debounces a request to onRequestAssist if conditions are met.
divergences.iosBehavior: User must manually tap 'Suggest details' (if implemented) to trigger assist.
divergences.fix: Implement auto-assist detection in iOS TaskEditorSheet (monitor title/detail changes and auto-request after a debounce delay if assist is available).

divergences.description: Android TaskFormSheet has auto-apply assist suggestions for new tasks (lines 892-906) if a UI setting enables it; iOS has no auto-apply setting or logic.
divergences.androidBehavior: If autoApplyAssistEnabled && target is Add, automatically apply applicable suggestions (e.g., title, priority, schedule).
divergences.iosBehavior: All suggestions require manual taps to apply (via SmartFillPreviewCard 'Apply all').
divergences.fix: Add an optional auto-apply assist setting to iOS (if iOS supports such settings) and implement logic to automatically apply non-destructive suggestions.

divergences.description: Android TaskBulkImportSheet runs each candidate title through the smart-fill parser (line 441-449 in TaskScreen.kt onImport logic) to pre-fill scheduling, priority, and recurrence before creating tasks. iOS TaskBulkImportSheet does the same (lines 88-105 in TaskBulkImportSheet.swift).
divergences.androidBehavior: Each selected title is parsed by taskTitleSmartFill or equivalent; detected fields are set on the new task.
divergences.iosBehavior: Each selected title is parsed by parseSmartFill (line 95); detected fields populate dueDate, priority, recurrence.
divergences.fix: Verify both implementations are in sync. Ensure iOS applies all detected fields (priority, due date, target date, recurrence) consistently with Android.

divergences.description: Android TaskFormSheet shows 'Open the existing task instead' button (line 1119-1123) when a duplicate task name is detected; iOS has no such convenience action.
divergences.androidBehavior: onOpenExistingTask callback passed to sheet; button taps it with the title string.
divergences.iosBehavior: No button or flow to open existing task.
divergences.fix: Add callback to iOS TaskEditorSheet to open an existing task by title. Button should trigger this callback.

divergences.description: Android TaskItem rows are visually distinct from each other with spacing and ChronosListCard containers; iOS TaskRow items have no container or visual separation (just list rows).
divergences.androidBehavior: Each TaskItem wrapped in ChronosListCard with spacing/padding.
divergences.iosBehavior: List rows with default separator.
divergences.fix: Wrap iOS TaskRow in a card-like Surface or use list row custom styling to provide visual separation matching Android's ChronosListCard appearance.

area: Habits — streak tracking, consistency cards, missed-habit repair, habit lifecycle (complete/pause/skip/defer), list organization
androidFlow: Android (feature/habits/HabitScreen.kt): Main habits list is a scrollable LazyColumn. At top: header + 3 metric tiles (Active / Best streak / Done today) + Add button. Then HabitConsistencyCard (14-day bar chart with headline), HabitStreakChart (top-5 habits by streak as horizontal bars), HabitRepairPanel (AI suggestions card), then list of HabitRows. Each HabitRow: title + action icons (Edit/Archive) + status pills (Due/Paused/Cadence/Streak/Adherence/BestTime) + 7-day week strip (dots M–S) + deferred status + actions (Complete button, More button). HabitContextActionSheet modal for full lifecycle: Complete, Defer (1hr), Skip, Pause/Resume, Edit, Duplicate, Archive. HabitRepairPanel shows reason + time slot + source label (Smart/AI) + Complete button.
iosFlow: iOS (ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Habits/HabitsView.swift): Identical list structure (ScrollView + LazyVStack). Metric tiles at top (Active / Best streak / Done today). Habits present when non-empty. HabitCard: title + subtitle row (flame icon + streak, cadence, window, difficulty) + optional deferred note + 7-day week strip + status pills + Quick-complete circle button. Repair panel uses ChronosGlassCard (vs Android's ChronosListCard), shows "Schedule at" label + time range + source label (On-device AI / Smart). Actions differ: HabitCard has inline circle-complete button visible; full lifecycle (defer/skip/pause) accessible via HabitContextActionSheet (.medium/.large sheet). Editor uses List form (Form, Picker sections) — not a bottom sheet.

divergences.description: HabitCard structure and visual hierarchy differ. Android displays status as inline pills below a text summary. iOS shows flame icon + streak + cadence + window + difficulty in one subtitle row, then separate status pills row. iOS adds visible circle-complete button inline, Android keeps it in action row below.
divergences.androidBehavior: HabitRow displays title, then FlowRow of status pills (Due/Paused/Cadence/Streak/Adherence), then window info and difficulty as separate Text line, then weekstrip, then action buttons (Complete, More) at bottom.
divergences.iosBehavior: HabitCard shows title, then one subtitle row with flame+streak, cadence, window, difficulty all inline with labels+icons. Status pills displayed separately below weekstrip. Large circular complete button (doneToday ? filled checkmark : empty circle) always visible top-right, alongside ellipsis menu.
divergences.fix: Restructure iOS HabitCard subtitle to match Android's text-only format: remove the flame icon and integrated labels from the subtitle row. Move streak display to status pills row. Make complete action (filled pill or dedicated button below title) not a large circle button. Keep the icons and inline completeness indication, but restructure the visual organization to primary-text→pills→weekstrip→actions pattern matching Android.

divergences.description: Missed-habit repair suggestion text layout differs. Android shows reason + time range in one line ('${reason}. HH:MM-HH:MM'). iOS shows reason on separate line, then time range on its own line prefixed with 'Schedule at'.
divergences.androidBehavior: Text combines reason and suggested time in a single bodySmall line: '${suggestion.reason}. ${formatDisplayMinute(suggestedStartMinute)}-${formatDisplayMinute(suggestedEndMinute)}'. Source label displayed separately below on a third line (labelSmall, primary color).
divergences.iosBehavior: Suggestion laid out vertically: title, reason, then HStack with 'Schedule at HH:MM–HH:MM' label (systemImage: calendar.badge.plus) and source label on same line right-aligned.
divergences.fix: iOS repair suggestion layout should condense to Android's pattern: combine reason + time on one line ('${reason}. ${startMinute}-${endMinute}'), remove the 'Schedule at' prefix and calendar icon, and place source label on its own line below, matching Android's label styling.

divergences.description: Repair panel container styling: Android uses ChronosListCard (opaque card), iOS uses ChronosGlassCard with primary tint. The card styling and surrounding visual treatment differs.
divergences.androidBehavior: HabitRepairPanel wrapped in ChronosListCard with standard card styling. Header row: AutoFixHigh icon + 'Missed-habit repair' title.
divergences.iosBehavior: HabitRepairPanel wrapped in ChronosGlassCard(tint: brandPrimary) with glass/frosted appearance and tint coloring. Header uses wand.and.stars icon instead of AutoFixHigh.
divergences.fix: Change iOS repair panel container from ChronosGlassCard to ChronosListCard (or equivalent opaque card). Change icon from 'wand.and.stars' to 'AutoFixHigh' (or equivalent Material icon). Remove the tint parameter so the card matches Android's neutral styling.

divergences.description: Habit editor surface and interaction model: Android shows an expanded bottom sheet (ChronosFormBottomSheet, large compact expandable form). iOS shows a NavigationStack inside a sheet with List-based Form, supporting edit mode for existing habits. iOS supports edit mode (passing existing habit), Android uses separate Edit vs Add sheet targets.
divergences.androidBehavior: HabitFormSheet is a composable that receives HabitSheetTarget (Add with optional prefillTitle, or Edit with habit). Displays a full bottom sheet with cadence picker, difficulty slider, time window picker, linked goal, schedule recurrence picker, templates, history hints, etc.
divergences.iosBehavior: HabitEditorSheet receives optional habit (for editing) or initialTitle (for adding). Uses NavigationStack → Form with DatePicker (for times), Slider, Toggle, Picker sections. When habit is non-nil, edits existing; when nil, creates new. Uses .presentationDetents([.medium, .large]).
divergences.fix: iOS HabitEditorSheet's edit mode and date/time picker need alignment check: verify that Android's time-window picker (ChronosTimeWindowControls showing minute-of-day intervals) matches iOS's DatePicker (hour + minute). Ensure both support the same cadence/recurrence presets and schedule options. iOS appears to have edit support but Android's code paths should be verified to match; if iOS supports edit and Android does via separate edit target, that's compatible but document the difference.

divergences.description: Habit lifecycle access pattern: Android shows all actions in a context-action-sheet modal (Complete, Defer, Skip, Pause/Resume, Edit, Archive). iOS shows same actions but in a List-based sheet with separate sections (lifecycle actions, edit/duplicate/archive). Context menu accessed via 'More' button on Android, ellipsis + onMore callback on iOS.
divergences.androidBehavior: HabitRow displays 'More' button that opens HabitContextActionSheet (ChronosModalBottomSheet). Actions laid out as full-width buttons: Complete, Defer, Skip, Pause/Resume, Edit, Archive.
divergences.iosBehavior: HabitCard displays ellipsis button top-right that sets contextHabit, triggering HabitContextActionSheet (NavigationStack + List with Sections). Same actions but in List rows with structured sections (lifecycle, edit, destructive archive).
divergences.fix: iOS structure is functionally equivalent but uses List UI instead of stacked buttons. This is acceptable iOS convention, but ensure all actions (Complete, Defer, Skip, Pause/Resume, Edit, Archive, Duplicate) are present and functional. Verify button order and grouping match Android's mental model (actions on top, edit/manage in middle, archive at bottom as destructive).

divergences.description: Week-strip dot sizing and layout: Android uses Box (16dp x 16dp, RoundedCornerShape(6.dp)) with filled/empty background. iOS uses Circle (10x10) with optional strokeBorder overlay for today. Visual appearance is subtly different (square-ish vs circular).
divergences.androidBehavior: HabitWeekStrip displays 7 days as a Row of Boxes (16dp size, 6dp corner radius, filled with primary/todayEmpty/empty colors). Day initial shown below as Text (labelSmall, black/gray).
divergences.iosBehavior: Displays 7 days as VStacks of Circles (10dp diameter) with optional strokeBorder (1.5pt primary color when today). Day initial shown below as Text (system size 9pt).
divergences.fix: iOS week strip should use 16dp squares with 6dp corner radius (RoundedRectangle) instead of 10dp circles. This matches the visual density and squarer aesthetic of Android's week strip. Ensure color values (filled=brandSecondary, todayEmpty=brandSecondary.opacity(0.28), empty=outline.opacity(0.22)) align with Android's primary/todayEmpty/empty palette.

divergences.description: Consistency card and streak chart cards: Android uses ChronosListCard, iOS uses ChronosGlassCard. The card container styling differs significantly (opaque vs frosted glass).
divergences.androidBehavior: ConsistencyCard and StreakChart both wrapped in ChronosListCard. Standard opaque card appearance.
divergences.iosBehavior: ConsistencyCard and StreakChartCard both wrapped in ChronosGlassCard. Frosted glass appearance with semi-transparency.
divergences.fix: Change iOS ConsistencyCard and StreakChartCard from ChronosGlassCard to ChronosListCard to match Android's opaque card styling. This is a visual consistency change across the habits list.

androidFlow: Android (feature/goals/): Goals is a full standalone screen route (ChronosRoute.Goals) opened via cross-section navigation from the shell. It's NOT a tab inside DayDialScreen. Accessed via: (1) QuickAdd menu → "New goal" command, or (2) bottom-bar shell navigation (when expanded via navigation rail on tablets). The feature is module-optional (goalsEnabled flag) and fully managed by GoalViewModel with reactive updates to goal list and linked-work counts via composable state management.
iosFlow: iOS (ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Goals/): Goals is a TabSection member under "Track" inside a flat Tab(View).sidebarAdaptable structure. It is a top-level navigation destination (equivalent to Tasks, Habits, etc.), NOT integrated into DayDialScreen. Accessed via: RootView tabShell → .goals tab selection. Feature toggles on/off in Settings (settings.goalsEnabled). Linked work is queried live via @Query on TaskItem/Habit filtered by goalID; goal list via @Query<Goal>; no formal ViewModel layer — SwiftData models directly expose save/delete via modelContext.

divergences.description: Android: Goals is a cross-section destination (accessed via shell navigation or QuickAdd command). iOS: Goals is a TabSection member nested under 'Track' in a flat TabView, with no integration into the Plan/Today/Focus triad.
divergences.androidBehavior: Goals opened via ChronosRoute.Goals from the shell's back-stack navigation. Can be launched with prefilled data (e.g., capture text from QuickAdd).
divergences.iosBehavior: Goals accessed via $selection = .goals in RootView.tabShell. No support for pre-filled launch data from QuickAdd.
divergences.fix: Lift Goals to a dedicated tab in RootView.tabShell (not nested in TabSection), so it becomes a primary shell destination. Accept a 'prefill' state in GoalsView via .onOpenURL or environment injection to mirror Android's initialAddCapture parameter. Route QuickAdd 'New goal' → selection = .goals (already works for tab switch, but lacks capture prefill). Files: ios/ChronosFlow/App/RootView.swift, ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Goals/GoalsView.swift.

divergences.description: Android: Goal list is a single scrollable screen with Active/Completed sections, metric tiles, optional overdue banner, and optional category filter row. iOS: Same layout, but accessed as a separate TabSection member instead of a primary shell destination.
divergences.androidBehavior: GoalScreen renders in-place with all sections (metrics, filter, active list, completed section with show/hide toggle). The screen is a full destination so the back stack can push/pop it.
divergences.iosBehavior: GoalsView renders the same layout (metrics, filter, sections), but as part of a tab (not a back-stack destination). No explicit 'back' button; tab switch is the navigation mechanism.
divergences.fix: Move Goals from TabSection('Track') to a top-level Tab at the same level as Plan/Today/Focus/Tasks. Preserve the existing GoalsView layout. This aligns iOS with Android's 'Goals is a full destination' model. File: ios/ChronosFlow/App/RootView.swift lines 88-98.

divergences.description: Android: +1 increment button in GoalCard calls onIncrement, which triggers viewModel.adjustProgress(goal, 1). iOS: +1 and -1 buttons directly mutate goal.progressValue in the onTapGesture closure. No validation that the adjusted value stays within 0...targetValue bounds during the edit.
divergences.androidBehavior: GoalCard onClick → onIncrement callback → GoalViewModel.adjustProgress(goal, delta) → clamps to 0..targetValue in the ViewModel, then saves via goalRepository.
divergences.iosBehavior: GoalCard button → adjust() closure → goal.progressValue = max(0, min(next, max(targetValue, 0))) → try? context.save(). The clamping logic is identical to Android, but happens inline in the View, not in a ViewModel.
divergences.fix: No change needed — the iOS implementation correctly clamps progress. However, for consistency with Android's ViewModel-driven pattern, optionally lift the adjust() logic into a computed property or a lightweight ViewModel so it's testable and consistent with Android architecture. If this is low-priority, the current GoalCard implementation is functionally correct. Files: ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Goals/GoalsView.swift lines 221-228 (adjust function).

divergences.description: Android: Goal metric tiles show 'Active' and 'Completed' counts in a 2-column row. iOS: Same layout (MetricTile with value/label), but uses ChronosGlassCard tone/tint instead of Android's ChronosMetricTile component styling.
divergences.androidBehavior: ChronosMetricTile (from core/ui/components) renders count and label with a specific design. iOS MetricTile is a custom local struct inside GoalsView.
divergences.iosBehavior: MetricTile is a private struct in GoalsView using ChronosGlassCard(tone: .quiet, tint:...). Visual style differs from Android's shared component.
divergences.fix: Extract the iOS MetricTile into a shared ChronosCore component (ios/ChronosCore/Sources/.../MetricTile.swift) and mirror the Android ChronosMetricTile's appearance so reuse is consistent across screens. Alternatively, confirm both implementations' visual output are equivalent via screenshots. Current implementation is functionally equivalent. Files: ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Goals/GoalsView.swift lines 233-246 (MetricTile).

divergences.description: Android: Category filter row only shows once 2+ categories are in use (checked via remember(goals) { goalCategoriesInUse(goals) }). iOS: Same logic, but the filter chip selection works differently — clicking 'All' clears selectedCategory, and re-clicking a category toggles it off.
divergences.androidBehavior: ChronosOptionChips with selected / onSelected callback. Filter is exclusive: selecting a category sets it, 'All' clears the filter.
divergences.iosBehavior: FilterChip is a toggle: tapping 'All' sets selectedCategory = nil, tapping a category toggles selectedCategory = (category == selected) ? nil : category. This means tapping a category twice deselects it (toggle), not re-filtering.
divergences.fix: Change the FilterChip toggle logic in iOS to match Android's exclusive selection (no toggle-off on re-tap). Replace lines 126-130 in GoalsView.swift: change `selectedCategory = (selectedCategory == cat) ? nil : cat` to `selectedCategory = cat` so re-tapping the same category does NOT deselect it. This matches Android's ChronosOptionChips behavior. File: ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Goals/GoalsView.swift lines 126-130.

divergences.description: Android: GoalFormSheet accepts a prefillTitle parameter on add and can suggest a category/target from keywords/numbers in the title. iOS: GoalEditorSheet uses SwiftUI Form and supports category suggestions and target extraction. Both have nearly identical logic, but iOS's implementation is inside GoalsView as a struct instead of a shared module.
divergences.androidBehavior: GoalFormSheet is a composable in the feature module. Keyword suggestions and target extraction live in GoalFormSheet.kt helpers (suggestGoalCategory, goalTargetFromTitle, etc.). iOS port mirrors this via GoalLabels in ChronosCore.
divergences.iosBehavior: GoalEditorSheet is defined inside GoalsView.swift and uses GoalLabels (from ChronosCore) for all helpers. The form layout matches Android exactly (title, description, category chips with custom entry, target with quick picks, collapsible Details for date/notes). Feature parity is complete.
divergences.fix: No change needed — iOS has full feature parity with Android via GoalLabels. Both support: category suggestions (suggestGoalCategory), target extraction from title (goalTargetFromTitle), deadline presets (goalDeadlinePresets), and warnings (goalTargetBelowProgressWarning, goalTargetDateWarning). All helpers are shared in ChronosCore.

divergences.description: Android: GoalDetailSheet shows linked tasks/habits fetched via GoalViewModel.detailLinkedWork (a StateFlow<GoalLinkedWork>). iOS: GoalDetailView uses @Query filters on TaskItem/Habit by goalID and recomputes counts live.
divergences.androidBehavior: GoalViewModel.detailLinkedWork emits GoalLinkedWork with tasks/habits. Detail sheet opens when detailGoalId is set; closing clears it. Use case: ObserveGoalLinkedWorkUseCase(goalId).
divergences.iosBehavior: GoalDetailView's init sets up @Query filters (goalID == goal.id). Linked tasks/habits update reactively as TaskItem/Habit rows change. No explicit ViewModel needed; SwiftData handles the live refresh.
divergences.fix: No change needed — iOS correctly queries linked work reactively. iOS's @Query approach is equivalent to Android's observeGoalLinkedWorkUseCase (both re-run when linked data changes). Both show the same detail header (progress bar, total, linked-work hint) and task/habit rows with completion/streak state.

divergences.description: Android: Completed goals are behind a show/hide toggle (rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }). iOS: showCompleted toggle is also present (line 21), but defaults to true instead of false, so completed goals are visible by default.
divergences.androidBehavior: Completed goals section has a Show/Hide button that defaults to hidden (false).
divergences.iosBehavior: Completed goals section has a Show/Hide button that defaults to visible (true).
divergences.fix: Change iOS default from true to false to match Android. File: ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Goals/GoalsView.swift line 21, change `@State private var showCompleted = true` to `@State private var showCompleted = false`.

divergences.description: Android: Empty state for a goal with no linked work shows via ChronosEmptyState in GoalDetailSheet. iOS: Uses a ChronosGlassCard with Label + Icon instead of the screen-level ChronosEmptyState.
divergences.androidBehavior: GoalDetailSheet shows ChronosEmptyState (title, message) when linkedWork.isEmpty is true.
divergences.iosBehavior: GoalDetailView's emptyState var renders a ChronosGlassCard with Label('No linked work yet', systemImage: 'link').
divergences.fix: Ensure the iOS empty-state visual matches Android's style. Current iOS version (Label + ChronosGlassCard) is visually distinct from Android's ChronosEmptyState. For consistency, update iOS to use a matching component or confirm both convey the same information. No functional change needed. File: ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Goals/GoalDetailView.swift lines 94-105 (emptyState).

androidFlow: Android's medication access is routed via `ChronosNavigationState.navigateToMedication()` (app/src/main/java/com/ChronosFlow/VBCR/navigation/MedicationAccess.kt), which delegates to `ChronosRoute.Medication()` in the nav stack. The medication screen itself is wrapped in `SensitiveRouteGate` (app/src/main/java/com/ChronosFlow/VBCR/navigation/SensitiveRouteGate.kt) that gates access behind biometric/passcode auth when `SensitiveArea.MEDICATION` protection is enabled. The gate handles canAuthenticate=false by failing open (rendering content with a warning banner) rather than permanently locking the user out. The MedicationScreen is a single full-screen composable displaying an ordered list of active plans via LazyColumn, with medication-specific actions (mark taken/missed, snooze, skip, pause/resume, archive) accessible both inline in each card and via a context action sheet. The screen integrates AI-assisted suggestion panels (adherence suggestions, auto-assist for new entries), adherence analytics (7/14-day trend, on-track days), and refill warnings.
iosFlow: iOS's medication access is implemented via a `.medicationLock()` view modifier on MedicationView (ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Medication/MedicationView.swift:53), which calls `sensitiveGate(.medication)` to delegate to `SensitiveAreaGate` (ios/ChronosFlow/Security/AppLock.swift). The gate is identical in intent (biometric/passcode + fail-open) and uses the same `SensitiveArea` enum. However, MedicationView is not a standalone screen — it is embedded as one of many tabs in the root `TabView(.sidebarAdaptable)` within RootView (ios/ChronosFlow/App/RootView.swift:88-101). The medication list is a scrollable LazyVStack with per-plan cards (MedicationCard) and per-plan adherence cards (MedicationAdherenceCard) stacked sequentially, rather than a single unified layout. The view lacks several Android features: no adherence suggestion panel (AI-driven reminder optimization), no quick-add chips for empty state, no explicit multi-time reminder UI (though the data model supports reminderMinutes array), and dose/refill actions are surfaced via context menu rather than an explicit context action sheet. The editor is a modal sheet (MedicationEditorSheet) rather than inline form handling.

divergences.description: Android's MedicationScreen is a single cohesive page (LazyColumn) with cards for metrics, add button, next-dose card, refill card, adherence chart, adherence suggestion panel, and medication list — all vertically ordered. iOS's MedicationView is a single scrollable stack (LazyVStack) but splits adherence data into per-plan `MedicationAdherenceCard` items stacked after each `MedicationCard`, creating a 2N layout (medication + adherence per plan) instead of a unified metric/list structure.
divergences.androidBehavior: MedicationScreen renders: (1) header, (2) metric tiles (Active, Taken 7d, Missed), (3) Add button, (4) next-dose card (if plans exist), (5) refill card (if any low supply), (6) adherence chart (if any history), (7) adherence suggestion panel (if suggestions exist), (8) per-plan MedicationRow cards in a list.
divergences.iosBehavior: MedicationView renders: (1) refill summary card (if any low supply), (2) alternating MedicationCard + MedicationAdherenceCard pairs for each plan. No unified metric tiles, no add button in the hierarchy, no next-dose card, no adherence suggestion panel. Metric tiles and add button are handled at the toolbar level (navigationTitle, toolbar items).
divergences.fix: Reorganize iOS MedicationView to match Android's layout: (1) Add ChronosPageHeader equivalent (title + subtitle), (2) Insert metric tiles (Active count, Taken 7d from aggregated doseEvents, Missed count) as a single HStack of ChronosMetricTile equivalents, (3) Add a FilledTonalButton for 'Add Medication', (4) Add MedicationNextDoseCard (if plans not empty) showing upcoming dose across all plans, (5) Keep RefillSummaryCard in place, (6) Add MedicationAdherenceChart showing aggregated 14-day trend, (7) Add AdherenceSuggestionPanel when suggestions exist (currently missing), (8) List only MedicationCard items (remove per-plan adherence stacking; surface adherence inline via pills/info within each card). File: ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Medication/MedicationView.swift.

divergences.description: Android's `MedicationViewModel.adherenceSuggestions` flow and `MedicationAdherencePanel` compose a proactive AI-driven suggestion UI that recommends reminder time adjustments based on adherence patterns. iOS MedicationView has NO adherence suggestion panel at all — the model supports the data structures (MedicationAdherence tracking) but the UI does not surface suggestions.
divergences.androidBehavior: MedicationScreen conditionally renders `MedicationAdherencePanel` when `adherenceSuggestions.isNotEmpty()`, displaying up to 3 suggestions with 'Apply' / 'Dismiss' buttons. Suggestions come from `medicationAdherenceAssistPlanner.suggestAdjustments()` (line 145 in MedicationViewModel.kt), which scores reminder times against actual adherence patterns and proposes a better minute-of-day. ApplyAdherenceSuggestion() updates the reminder time via the standard updateMedication() path.
divergences.iosBehavior: MedicationView has no suggestion panel. No calls to adherence assistant, no UI to surface or apply suggestions. The capability simply does not exist.
divergences.fix: Implement adherence suggestion panel in iOS. (1) Add a property to store suggestions (e.g., [MedicationAdherenceSuggestion]) computed or observed from adherence analysis (mirror Android's `medicationAdherenceAssistPlanner`). (2) Render a suggestion card in MedicationView's LazyVStack (after the metric tiles, before the plan list) when suggestions are non-empty, matching the visual style of Android's MedicationAdherencePanel. (3) Wire 'Apply' to call an update on the selected plan's reminderMinuteOfDay, and 'Dismiss' to remove that suggestion from the list. This requires either a new assistant module or stub logic that mirrors the Android planner's interface. File: ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Medication/MedicationView.swift.

divergences.description: Android's medication list shows per-plan adherence metrics inline as small pill-shaped info badges (MedicationInfoPill: Reminder, Adherence %, Form, Paused/Refill status), with an expandable details section. iOS's MedicationCard is simpler — it shows a single 'Take' button and summary text (dose · times), plus a separate MedicationAdherenceCard per plan with a 7/14-day rate breakdown. Android also renders a low-supply warning banner inline within the expanded section; iOS splits this into a RefillSummaryCard at the top.
divergences.androidBehavior: Per-plan card (MedicationRow): header (icon, name, form icon, optional 'Low Supply' badge), dosage, FlowRow of info pills (Reminder time emphasized, Adherence %, Form, Status/Refill with optional alert styling), Edit/Archive/Expand icons. Expanded section adds: refill details, notes, recent dose event, Skip/Pause-Resume buttons. Low-supply inline warning banner (red border, error color) renders conditionally within the card.
divergences.iosBehavior: Per-plan card (MedicationCard): HStack of icon, VStack of name, schedule summary (dose · times), meal timing label, max-doses label, paused-until label, refill-in-N-days label, and a simple 'Take' button. Separate MedicationAdherenceCard per plan: 7/14-day rates, on-track count, adherence trend chart, recent dose history list. Refill warning is a top-level RefillSummaryCard listing all low-supply plans.
divergences.fix: Consolidate iOS MedicationCard to match Android's visual density and pill-based metadata: (1) Add MedicationInfoPill (or equivalent) components to show Reminder, Adherence %, Form, Status, and Refill status inline (not in a separate card). (2) Add an expand/collapse toggle to reveal Skip/Pause-Resume buttons and notes (currently in context menu). (3) Inline the low-supply warning banner (red border, conditional rendering) within the expanded card section. (4) Move adherence rate/chart into the expanded section or into the pill metadata to avoid stacking a full adherence card per medication.
