area: Focus timer & sessions (block-bounded split phases, Live Activity, preset configs)
androidFlow: Android enters focus from Plan tab (on-block chips start focus with presets) or Today tab (current-block start). The in-app FocusDayDialFocusDelegate manages FocusExecutionState with phases list, currentPhaseIndex, awaitingPhaseAdvance. At each phase boundary, the session PAUSES (awaitingPhaseAdvance=true) and holds until user taps "Continue" (advancePhase()). Split presets: No breaks (flat), 25·5, 50·10, 30·5. FocusPhasePlanner divides block into cycles then fills remainder. Phase indicator shows dots (active/done/upcoming). Live Activity mirrors per-phase state via segmented bars, controls (Pause/Stop/+5m), and phase count. Split sessions persisted via FocusSplitSessionStore (SharedPreferences) so a kill mid-phase restores full plan.
iosFlow: iOS enters focus ONLY from Today tab (prefilledBlockID), never from Plan—users must navigate out of Plan, into Focus, then manually start. No direct "Start Focus" button on Plan blocks. FocusTimerModel is a singleton with planFocusPhases(blockMinutes:preset:) that builds phase list on start(). Holds at phase boundary (awaitingPhaseAdvance=true) but UI shows "Phase complete" / "Block complete" text, not prompting the next phase name (no "Time for a 5m break — tap to continue" copy like Android). Presets: noBreaks (flat), p25_5 (25·5), p50_10 (50·10), p30_5 (30·5)—same denominators but different enum names. Phase dots rendered with simple 12pt / 8pt size swap, no "pulse on active" bounce animation. Live Activity via FocusSegmentedBar renders color-coded segments. Split snapshots persisted in SwiftData (via saveSnapshot() → ChronosStore). Extend-only (+5m / +15m) controls, no -5m shorten (clamped to min(5)). Mid-session break injection offers 5/10/15m presets. No "Skip phase" affordance in UI (skipPhase() exists in model but not exposed).

divergences.description: iOS can only enter focus from Today tab (via prefilledBlockID when tapping a current block). Android allows entry from BOTH Plan tab (inline chips on blocks) AND Today tab (quick-action on current block). On iOS, Plan tab blocks have no direct Focus start—users must leave Plan, open Focus tab, then manually pick a block.
divergences.androidBehavior: Plan tab blocks show 'Start focus' / 'Mark complete' buttons inline. User can choose split preset and launch focus immediately from the dial or list. Today tab current block also has quick-launch.
divergences.iosBehavior: Plan tab block editor (tap block) has no focus entry—only edit/delete/context. Must navigate to Focus tab (separate destination), then manually select a block and start.
divergences.fix: Add a 'Start Focus' button or secondary action on Plan-tab blocks (inline in BlockRow or via context menu) that navigates to Focus tab and pre-fills the blockID, mirroring Android's DayDialFocusTab.onStart() bridge.

divergences.description: Android FocusTab shows boundary prompts naming the NEXT phase ('Time for a 5m break — tap to continue' / 'Back to focus for 25m — tap to continue'). iOS FocusTimerModel computes a generic boundary prompt but FocusView shows only 'Phase complete' / 'Block complete', losing semantic guidance about what's next.
divergences.androidBehavior: When awaitingPhaseAdvance: focusBoundaryPrompt() renders 'Time for {minutes}m {kind} — tap to continue', computed from focusSession.nextPhase.
divergences.iosBehavior: boundaryPrompt computed in FocusTimerModel (focusPhaseBoundaryText) but FocusView displays only hardcoded 'Phase complete' / 'Block complete' if timer.nextPhase != nil.
divergences.fix: Replace hardcoded text in FocusView.boundaryControls with timer.boundaryPrompt ?? 'Phase complete' to surface the Android prompt copy (mirrors focusPhaseBoundaryText from ChronosCore).

divergences.description: Android phase dots scale smoothly (10dp → 8dp inactive, animated with navIndicator easing) and pulse on active. iOS dots swap 12pt ↔ 8pt with a bouncy animation, but no continuous pulse on the current phase. The visual emphasis is weaker.
divergences.androidBehavior: FocusPhaseIndicator renders 10.dp size, animates active → 0.8 scale, with color alpha transitions. Active dot stays full brightness.
divergences.iosBehavior: FocusView.phaseDots renders 12pt current / 8pt other, animates with .bouncy timing. No pulse or continuous glow on the current phase.
divergences.fix: Add a .symbolEffect(.pulse, isActive: true) modifier to the active phase dot in FocusView.phaseDots, and adjust sizing to match Android (10dp slot, 0.8 scale inactive) for consistency.

divergences.description: Android expose skipFocusSession() via Skip button on the Play/Pause row (when linked to a block). iOS FocusView has skipPhase() in FocusTimerModel but no UI button to invoke it. Users cannot skip phases on iOS.
divergences.androidBehavior: Skip button (⏭) shown when session is linked to a block and not awaiting phase advance. Calls onSkip → viewModel.skipFocusSession().
divergences.iosBehavior: skipPhase() method exists but unreachable. FocusView.runningControls has no skip button.
divergences.fix: Add a skip button to FocusView.runningControls (icon: 'forward.fill', label: 'Skip phase') that calls timer.skipPhase(), visible only when timer.isSplitSession && timer.phase != .idle && !timer.awaitingPhaseAdvance.

divergences.description: Android allows both extending (+15m) and shortening (-15m) the current phase via onExtend/onShorten. iOS FocusTimerModel.extend() clamps to positive, so shorten is a silent no-op; FocusView only shows +5m / +15m controls, no -5m option.
divergences.androidBehavior: FocusTab renders two rows: '+5m' and '-5m' buttons (onAdjustByMinutes), both functional. onExtend(15) and onShorten(15) change the active phase and update Live Activity.
divergences.iosBehavior: adjustControls shows +5m and +15m only. No minus buttons. extend(minutes: -5) would clamp to 5 (no-op), so -5m is intentionally hidden.
divergences.fix: Add '-5m' and '-15m' buttons to FocusView.adjustControls, wired to timer.extend(minutes: -5) and timer.extend(minutes: -15) with clamping in FocusTimerModel.extend() to max(5, current + delta).

divergences.description: Android FocusSplitSessionStore persists split snapshots in SharedPreferences (keyed 'chronos_focus_split_session') so a process kill mid-phase restores the full plan. iOS saves snapshots via saveSnapshot() → SwiftData (ChronosStore), but the persistence mechanism is less explicit and lacks the same cold-start recovery flow (restoreActiveSplitFromStore).
divergences.androidBehavior: SharedPreferencesFocusSplitSessionStore.save() encodes phases as 'F25,B5' string, persists on every state change when RUNNING/PAUSED. On app restart, DayDialFocusDelegate.restoreActiveSplitFromStore() checks if idle, loads snapshot, and restores phase plan.
divergences.iosBehavior: FocusTimerModel.saveSnapshot() encodes the same 'F25,B5' format and writes via UserDefaults(appGroup). No explicit restoreActiveSplitFromStore() hook. Snapshot is queried lazily (if active and has context).
divergences.fix: Add an explicit restoreActiveSplitFromStoreonAppear hook in FocusView (or FocusTimerModel.init) that checks if idle and snapshotContext != nil, loads the saved snapshot, and restores the full phasePlan before presenting idle UI—mirrors Android's restoreActiveSplitFromStore() pattern.

divergences.description: Android includes checkPhaseBoundary() called on each timer tick to auto-detect when the current phase elapses and transition to awaitingPhaseAdvance. iOS reachPhaseBoundary() is private and triggered only from the ticker's tick() method. No explicit hook for recovering mid-phase if the app is backgrounded and returns after phase boundary.
divergences.androidBehavior: DayDialFocusDelegate.checkPhaseBoundary() is called per tick, checks focusRemainingSeconds() > 0, and auto-pauses at boundary.
divergences.iosBehavior: FocusTimerModel.tick() checks remaining <= 0 and calls reachPhaseBoundary(), but there's no recovery hook if the app was backgrounded across a boundary.
divergences.fix: Add a .onAppear hook in FocusView that calls a new FocusTimerModel.recoverBoundaryIfNeeded() method, which checks if the phase should have elapsed while backgrounded and calls reachPhaseBoundary() to re-sync.

divergences.description: Android Live Activity shows phase count ('Phase 2/4') in both expanded and compact/minimal regions. iOS FocusLiveActivityWidget shows 'Phase N/M' in compact-trailing and dynamic-island expanded, but omits it from the lock-screen HStack, losing phase context on the main lock-screen widget.
divergences.androidBehavior: Live Activity displays phase progress persistently ('2 of 4', 'Phase 2/4').
divergences.iosBehavior: Lock screen shows block title + timer + segmented bar, but no phase count. Phase count appears only in Dynamic Island expanded.
divergences.fix: Add phase count to the iOS lock-screen tile in FocusLiveActivityWidget (after or below the timer), e.g., 'Phase \(context.state.phaseNumber)/\(context.state.totalPhases)' as a smaller caption.

divergences.description: Android FocusTab displays 'Paused · tap play to resume' label when status == PAUSED && !awaitingPhaseAdvance. iOS shows 'Paused' label but lacks the 'tap play to resume' helper text when the session is paused.
divergences.androidBehavior: Text('Paused · tap play to resume') shown below the timer ring when paused (but not at a boundary).
divergences.iosBehavior: FocusView shows Label('Paused', ...) with .transition(.opacity) but no 'tap play to resume' text.
divergences.fix: Change FocusView's pause label to match Android: 'Paused · tap play to resume' or expand the pause affordance with an explanatory caption.

androidFlow: Android: Sleep logging initiated from the quick-add FAB (in the dial shell) or from within the Today tab's "Log sleep" button. Tapping either opens SleepLogSheet (a modal sheet in the dial). The sheet displays: (1) Health Connect sync button at top, (2) Sleep quality slider (1-5 with emoji label), (3) Bed/wake time pickers, (4) Sleep duration with overnight tag/warnings, (5) Interruptions slider (0-10), (6) "Refreshed" rating (1-5 emoji selector), (7) Wind-down notes field, (8) Save button. Health Connect sync can run one-time from the sheet without enabling background import. Manually logged nights are never overwritten by imports.
iosFlow: iOS: Sleep logging is accessed three ways: (1) From the Quick-Add menu (select "Log sleep"), (2) From the Sleep tab (tap the + button), or (3) Inline from the Sleep tab's readiness banner (implied). It opens SleepLogSheet (a sheet modal) with a Form containing: (1) DatePicker for bedtime/wake (not minute sliders), (2) In-sheet one-time Apple Health sync button, (3) Live validation hints (window label, overnight tag, duration vs 8h target, short/long warnings), (4) Quality slider (1-5 with label), (5) Interruptions stepper (0-10), (6) Wind-down notes field. iOS is missing: the "Refreshed" rating (1-5 emoji selector), the readiness-derived quality pre-fill, and the emoji quality label in the same presentation style. The Sleep tab itself shows a readiness banner (derived from latest night's quality/interruptions/times), Apple Health card with toggle for background import, trends (last 14 nights), and a list of recent logged nights.

divergences.description: iOS Sleep is a top-level tab in the sidebar/tab bar, not accessed via dial quick-add menu alone. The quick-add menu has a 'Log sleep' option, but the entry point is ambiguous vs Android's clear FAB → Sleep Log Sheet.
divergences.androidBehavior: Sleep log is a modal sheet triggered only from quick-add FAB or Today tab's button, always modal and in-focus.
divergences.iosBehavior: Sleep log is both a tab AND reachable via quick-add menu. Users can approach it from multiple entry points: the Sleep tab itself, or via Quick-Add. The tab-first design means sleep tracking surfaces at top level, competing with block planning.
divergences.fix: iOS should NOT have Sleep as a top-level tab. Instead, demote it to the Track submenu (like Habits/Goals), and ensure Quick-Add → Log sleep is the primary modal entry point, mirroring Android's dial-centric model. Remove the Sleep tab from RootView.swift's TabView and keep it only in the Track TabSection.

divergences.description: iOS SleepLogSheet uses a Form with DatePicker (hour + minute selectors), while Android uses ChronosTimePickerField (explicit minute-of-day input). Android's approach is more direct for sleep logging.
divergences.androidBehavior: SleepLogSheet has ChronosTimePickerField for bed and wake times, displaying minute-of-day and allowing direct entry or scrolling selection.
divergences.iosBehavior: SleepLogSheet uses SwiftUI's DatePicker with .hourAndMinute components. This is less explicit for sleep tracking (no minute-of-day context) and doesn't visually mirror Android.
divergences.fix: Replace the DatePicker in SleepLogSheet with a custom time-picker component that shows minute-of-day (like Android's ChronosTimePickerField), allowing the user to see/edit the minute value directly alongside hour/minute selectors. Alternatively, add minute-of-day labels next to the DatePickers.

divergences.description: iOS is missing the 'Refreshed' rating field (1-5 emoji selector). Android's SleepLogSheetContent includes a 'How refreshed do you feel?' emoji row (RefreshedEmojiSelector) with 5 tappable emoji faces. iOS SleepLogSheet does not collect this data at all.
divergences.androidBehavior: RefreshedEmojiSelector displays 5 emoji faces (1-5 rating) below the interruptions slider. Users tap one to record how refreshed they feel the next morning. Data is saved as `refreshedRating` and flows to SleepTrack.
divergences.iosBehavior: SleepLogSheet has no refreshed rating collection. iOS SleepTrack model has no `refreshedRating` field (it has `windDownNotes` instead, which Android also has).
divergences.fix: Add a 'How refreshed do you feel?' row to the Quality section in SleepLogSheet (after the Interruptions stepper). Create an emoji selector matching Android's RefreshedEmojiSelector (5 tappable emoji buttons). Add a `refreshedRating: Int` field to ios/ChronosFlow/Models/Wellbeing.swift::SleepTrack. Save the rating when the sheet commits.

divergences.description: Android's sleep quality is labeled with emoji + text (e.g. '😴 3 of 5 · Light sleep') and matches the Android design pattern. iOS shows only a numeric slider without the emoji quality label in the same visual prominence.
divergences.androidBehavior: Quality slider is paired with a row displaying `sleepQualityEmoji(quality) + ' $quality of 5 · ' + sleepQualityLabel(quality)`, e.g. '😴 3 of 5 · Light sleep'.
divergences.iosBehavior: Quality slider displays as 'Quality: 3/5' and a separate Text with `SleepLogHints.qualityLabel(Int(quality))`, e.g. 'Light sleep'. The emoji is not shown in the quality row.
divergences.fix: Update the Quality slider row in SleepLogSheet to display emoji + label inline, matching Android: 'sleepQualityEmoji(Int(quality)) · 3/5 · qualityLabel(Int(quality))'. Use ChronosCore's quality label helpers (already being used) and add an emoji function to SleepLogHints or the quality label logic.

divergences.description: iOS SleepLogSheet's health sync button does NOT auto-populate fields after a successful sync in all cases. Android's HealthConnectSleepSyncButton fills in quality, start, and end times immediately when a night is synced.
divergences.androidBehavior: HealthConnectSleepSyncButton syncs last night from Health Connect, and the reactive sleepTrack stream populates the sheet's bed/wake/quality fields automatically when the import lands. Manual edits are preserved.
divergences.iosBehavior: SleepLogSheet has a one-time sync button. After sync, if a newer night is imported, it triggers autoPopulateFromLatestImport() which mirrors bed/wake/quality/interruptions. However, the Refreshed rating (when added) is not auto-populated from imports (Android doesn't do this either, but iOS should at least match the existing auto-fill scope).
divergences.fix: Ensure auto-population in SleepLogSheet::autoPopulateFromLatestImport() populates quality and interruptions the same way bed/wake are populated. Verify the one-time sync flow matches the reactive Android behavior (already appears to do so).

divergences.description: Android's main dial view includes an in-place readiness banner (derived from latest night's quality/interruptions/times via SleepReadinessCore). iOS has a readiness card on the Sleep tab, not on the main Today/Plan view.
divergences.androidBehavior: The dial's Today tab or main view likely surfaces a readiness banner derived from the latest night, informing the user's daily plan (e.g. 'Depleted' tints the view or shows lighter tasks).
divergences.iosBehavior: Readiness is surfaced only on the Sleep tab itself (via SleepView's readiness card), not on Today or Plan. The user must navigate to Sleep to see readiness status.
divergences.fix: Add a readiness card or banner to TodayView (the iOS analogue of Android's Today tab) showing the latest night's readiness (derived via SleepReadinessCore, already in the codebase). This allows the user to see their readiness state without navigating to the Sleep tab. Position it above or near the focus/task section.

divergences.description: Android's HealthConnectSleepCard in the Export Data / Settings panel has a toggle 'Import sleep automatically' and a button 'Import now', with a result message. iOS's SleepView has a toggle 'Enable Health import', a summary line 'Last imported <date>', a result summary, and a button 'Import from Health'. The wording and organization differ.
divergences.androidBehavior: AvailableControls shows: text row 'Import sleep automatically' with ChronosSwitch, optional lastResult text, and 'Import now' button. Both toggle and button are in the same card. Settings-owned toggle; button is on-demand.
divergences.iosBehavior: SleepView's Apple Health card shows: toggle 'Enable Health import' (only when not already enabled), 'Last imported <date>' line, optional result summary, and 'Import from Health' button. When enabled, the toggle vanishes and only button remains visible.
divergences.fix: Restructure the Apple Health card in SleepView to always show both the toggle and button (like Android), not conditionally hide the toggle. Ensure the result message and last-import timestamp are always visible (they are now, good). Align button label to 'Import now' for consistency with Android.

area: Journal (entry composition, history, guided prompts, mood, dictation, fitness tracking)
androidFlow:
Android (DayDialScreen + DayDial navigation shell):
- Journal is a SHEET target, not a screen tab. Quick-Add FAB → "Journal entry" menu item → opens JournalComposerSheet as a modal bottom sheet within DayDialScreen (ChronosRoute.Day.TARGET_JOURNAL).
- Separate sidebar page access: DayDialScreen sidebar → SidebarPage.JOURNAL → JournalPageRoute (full page).
- Composer lives in the same JournalEntryComposer component whether called from sheet or sidebar.
- History shows "X of Y reflections" when filtered (journalHistoryPageSummary).
- Entry lists collapse/expand via ChronosCollapsibleSection (the "Add details" disclosure group) with live summaries like "1 highlight · 8:00 AM · 2 photos".
- Calendar overview is inline in the history (not a separate card).
- Multi-day range creation for new entries (checkbox: "Apply to a range of days").
- AI insight card with modal-style interface (generate/regenerate/dismiss buttons in a card, not a sheet).
- Workouts imported from Health Connect as secondary points with id prefix "hc-workout-".
- Dictation: not prominently featured; on-device AI for grammar/expand is via a dropdown ✨ menu button on fields.
iosFlow:
iOS (RootView tab shell):
- Journal is a TAB in the "Track" section of TabView (.sidebarAdaptable), not a modal sheet or sidebar page.
- Quick-Add sheet routes to this tab via selection = .journal (no separate sheet composer).
- Composer is inline in the full JournalView (state-based; no separate sheet component).
- History shows "X of Y" badge only when a search is active; no expand/collapse affordance per day group.
- Entry lists are always expanded; sub-notes render as bullet lists within the card; no collapsible sections.
- Calendar overview is a prominent card with month nav, mood/workout filters, and a recap line below the grid.
- No multi-day range creation option for new entries.
- AI insight card opened via a toolbar button → full-screen sheet (AssistantSheet), not inline.
- Workouts imported from HealthKit with the same "hc-workout-" id prefix convention.
- Dictation: prominent DictationController with recording UI, button in the composer card (not a secondary menu).

divergences.description: Journal is accessed as a top-level Tab in iOS (in Track group), but on Android it is reached via a modal sheet (Quick-Add → 'Journal entry') or a sidebar page within DayDial. These are fundamentally different navigation trees.
divergences.androidBehavior: Quick-Add FAB menu → 'Journal entry' → ChronosRoute.Day.TARGET_JOURNAL → sheet over DayDialScreen. Or DayDialScreen sidebar → SidebarPage.JOURNAL → JournalPageRoute (full sidebar page). The composer (JournalComposerSheet / JournalPageRoute) uses the same JournalEntryComposer component.
divergences.iosBehavior: Tab bar → 'Journal' tab (in Track section) → JournalView is the full screen. Quick-Add sheet has no separate journal action; selecting 'Journal entry' just routes to the tab.
divergences.fix: Remove Journal from the Track TabSection in RootView. Create a separate sheet component (e.g., JournalEditorSheet) that mirrors Android's JournalComposerSheet behavior. Route Quick-Add 'Journal entry' action to present this sheet over the current tab rather than navigating to a new tab. Keep an optional sidebar/full-screen mode for tablets/landscape but make the default entry point a modal sheet for parity.

divergences.description: iOS shows all features (composer, history, calendar, insights) in one long scrollable view, while Android separates the composer (when from Quick-Add) as a modal sheet and reserves the full page for history.
divergences.androidBehavior: JournalComposerSheet is a ChronosModalBottomSheet containing only JournalEntryComposer (mood, reflection, time, photos, AI assist buttons). JournalPageRoute wraps JournalPageContent, which layers: header, new-entry card, calendar, insight card, point-adder card, workout-import card, and a full history list.
divergences.iosBehavior: JournalView is one unified view: header (Today's reflection + streak), composerCard (mood, reflection, highlights, time, photos, dictation, 'Save' button), pointsSection, workoutImportCard, aiInsightCard, calendarOverview, and historySection — all in a single ScrollView.
divergences.fix: Extract composerCard, pointsSection, workoutImportCard, and aiInsightCard into a separate modal sheet component (JournalEditorSheet). The root JournalView should show: header (stats), calendar overview, and history only. The editor sheet overlays the root view when creating/editing an entry.

divergences.description: iOS calls out to dictation as a first-class feature in the composer (DictationController, prominent mic button), while Android handles it as part of the text field + offers AI polish as a secondary menu (✨ button).
divergences.androidBehavior: JournalEntryComposer renders a main-note TextField with no built-in mic button. AI transforms (grammar fix, expand/rewrite) are offered via a dropdown ✨ menu on the reflection field and on each sub-note. Dictation is not visible in the composer UI.
divergences.iosBehavior: JournalView.composerCard includes a dictationButton that toggles DictationController recording. The button shows 'Listening...' when active and appends transcripts to the draft. No inline ✨ polish button; AI is accessed via a separate Assistant toolbar button that opens a full sheet.
divergences.fix: Add a dictationButton to the Android JournalEntryComposer that mirrors iOS behavior (toggle DictationController state, show recording indicator, append to draft on completion). Move AI transforms (grammar/expand) from the ✨ dropdown into a separate on-device assist facility (e.g., a bottom sheet or toolbar action), not inline with field editing.

divergences.description: iOS history list uses a simple header per day with no expand/collapse control and shows entry count only during search. Android uses an always-visible ChronosCollapsibleSection with a summary line ('1 highlight · 8:00 AM · 2 photos') under the day label.
divergences.androidBehavior: journalHistoryPageSummary returns a label like '5 reflections match'. Day groups are rendered with a day-label row, per-entry cells, and inline point-adder below the group. No collapsible sections; the entire history is always visible.
divergences.iosBehavior: historySection shows 'History' title + a search box. Each day group has a header showing the day name, emoji mood (if set), entry count (only if writtenCount > 1 and not during search). Each entry is a JournalHistoryCard in a loop. No collapsible sections, no inline point adders per day.
divergences.fix: Remove the day-group headers and day-level point adders from the history section. Keep the per-entry cards flat. Add a search result count ('X of Y') that matches Android's journalHistoryPageSummary. For consistency with Android's collapsible 'Add details' pattern, the history should not have expand/collapse affordances at the day level — iOS is already correct here.

divergences.description: iOS has no multi-day range option for new entries. Android's JournalEntryComposer offers a checkbox 'Apply to a range of days' that generates one entry per day from a start to end date.
divergences.androidBehavior: JournalEntryComposer: when composing a new entry (isNew == true), a checkbox 'Apply to a range of days' unlocks an end-date picker and displays a summary ('Adds 5 entries, one per day'). The save button text updates to 'Save N entries'.
divergences.iosBehavior: JournalView.save() always creates one entry for the current day (.now). No range picker, no multiday option.
divergences.fix: Add a toggle 'Apply to a range of days' in the iOS composer's disclosure group. When enabled, show an end-date picker. On save, create one entry per day from today to the selected end date by calling context.insert() in a loop and then save() once.

divergences.description: iOS shows the AI insight card inline with a toolbar button to open a separate full-screen sheet (AssistantSheet). Android shows the insight card inline in the history section with a 'Reflect on my recent entries' button that toggles the card's state.
divergences.androidBehavior: JournalInsightCard is a ChronosListCard that lives inside JournalPageContent. States: Idle (show 'Reflect on my recent entries' button), Loading (spinner), Ready (text + 'Regenerate' / 'Dismiss' buttons). All inline.
divergences.iosBehavior: aiInsightCard is inline and shows similar states, but the 'Reflect on recent entries' action calls generateInsight() which populates insight.state. There is also a toolbar aiInsightsToolbarItem button that sets showAIInsights = true, opening AssistantSheet in a separate full-screen sheet.
divergences.fix: Remove the toolbar button and AssistantSheet from RootView. Keep the aiInsightCard inline as in Android. The 'Reflect on recent entries' and 'Regenerate' buttons should only appear in the card, not in a separate sheet. The card itself can remain dismissable with a 'Dismiss' button.

divergences.description: iOS does not expose an 'Add a point' inline adder below each day group in history. Android offers a quick-capture field below each day's entries in the history list.
divergences.androidBehavior: JournalPageContent history list: after each day's entries (inside grouped.forEach), there is a JournalPointAdder(compact=true) that lets the user add a timed point to that specific day without opening the full composer.
divergences.iosBehavior: historySection loops through groupedHistory and renders JournalHistoryCard for each entry, but there is no inline adder. The only point-adder is the separate pointsSection card at the top of the view.
divergences.fix: Add a JournalPointAdder (or equivalent inline subtask-style input) below the last entry of each day group in the history loop (inside the VStack for each group). This should accept a body and optional time, then call addPoint() with the day's date.

divergences.description: iOS history entries always show a full expanded view of sub-notes, main note, and photos. Android entries in the history can be collapsed or expanded (via an expand/collapse button when the entry is long, showing 'Show more' / 'Show less').
divergences.androidBehavior: JournalHistoryRow: when the entry body is long (> 220 chars or 4+ newlines), a 'Show more' / 'Show less' button appears and toggles the expanded state, using maxLines = 3 vs. maxLines = nil.
divergences.iosBehavior: JournalHistoryCard: renders mainNote with lineLimit(expanded ? nil : 4), so it does show a collapsible button via isLong check. This is already correct and matches Android.
divergences.fix: No change needed; iOS already implements the expand/collapse behavior. Verify the threshold logic (220 chars, 4 newlines) is consistent with Android.

divergences.description: Android displays the calendar and recap inline in the history page (JournalCalendarCard + recap line). iOS shows a prominent calendar card with month navigation, mood/workout filter pills, and a recap line — but also groups history entries by day with headers showing the mood emoji and entry count.
divergences.androidBehavior: JournalPageContent: calendar is shown in JournalCalendarCard before the history. Each day in the history has a row showing 'Mon, Jun 16 · 2 entries' and no per-day recap.
divergences.iosBehavior: calendarOverview is a prominent ChronosGlassCard with month nav, filter pills, weekday headers, a grid, and a recap line ('avg 😄 Great · 8 days journaled · 3 workouts'). History day headers show dayLabel (Today or weekday/month/day) and writtenCount (only if > 1).
divergences.fix: No major change needed. iOS's calendar and recap are actually richer than Android's. Keep them as-is, but ensure the recap line logic matches Android's journalMonthRecapLabel (if it exists; verify against ChronosCore). The day-group headers in the history (with mood emoji and entry count) are a good iOS enhancement and do not conflict with Android semantics.

area: Insights / Review (Day/Week/Month rollups, category breakdown, severity-ranked findings, execution score, AI recommendations)
androidFlow: On Android, the Insights tab IS a primary in-dial tab (DayDialTab.INSIGHTS, labeled "Review" to users). It sits alongside Plan, Today, Focus within the DayDialMainContent (feature/daydial/src/main/java/com/ChronosFlow/VBCR/feature/daydial/DayDialMainContent.kt, lines 627-673). The tab renders InsightsTab which aggregates: day/week/month period switchable execution metrics (planned/actual/missed/drift), category breakdown with concentration analysis, severity-ranked findings from ChronosCore, AI recommendations (local + cloud), trends (mood/energy/habits/medication/sleep/screen-time via InsightsTrendSections), and a button to open the detailed DayReviewSheet. The period selector + section-filter pills allow users to narrow scope. Everything is in-place within the dial, swipeable alongside other primary tabs.
iosFlow: On iOS, Review is a separate top-level TabView destination (ShellTab.review in ios/ChronosFlow/App/RootView.swift, line 122), grouped under "Track" in the sidebar on iPad or flattened into the tab bar on iPhone. It is NOT part of the DayDialScreen (ios/ChronosFlow/Features/DayDial/DayDialScreen.swift). InsightsView.swift is a standalone NavigationStack with its own UI that duplicates Android's insights logic (period rollups, findings, recommendations, trends) but is rendered as an independent surface, not as a tab within the day context. There is a floating "Day review" button in the toolbar (line 171 of InsightsView) that opens a separate DayReviewSheet, but this is modal and outside the main insights surface. The entire Insights experience is decoupled from the Plan/Today/Focus tabs.

divergences.description: Android: Review is a primary tab (INSIGHTS) within DayDialScreen, rendered as one of the 4 swipeable in-dial tabs. iOS: Review is a separate top-level shell destination, not nested in DayDialScreen.
divergences.androidBehavior: DayDialTab.INSIGHTS is one of DayDialTab.primary (Plan, Today, Focus) + INSIGHTS. Lines 888–891 in DayDialMainContent.kt assign tab indices 0–3. InsightsTab is composed directly inside the DayDialMainContent layout alongside Plan/Today/Focus (lines 627–673).
divergences.iosBehavior: ShellTab.review is a sibling to ShellTab.today, ShellTab.plan, ShellTab.focus at the top level of TabView (RootView.swift line 122). InsightsView is a standalone NavigationStack rendered outside DayDialScreen.
divergences.fix: Move InsightsView content into DayDialScreen as a fourth primary tab. Create an enum DayDialTab variant for INSIGHTS (already exists in Android, map to it). Render InsightsView as a @ViewBuilder closure passed to DayDialScreen, composed via an AnimatedContent or TabView within DayDialScreen to mirror DayDialMainContent's four swipeable tabs. Update RootView to render DayDialScreen hosting all four tabs, with Review no longer a separate shell destination.

divergences.description: Android: The Insights page is a unified scrollable surface with period selector, section-filter pills, and all insights sections (Execution, Categories, Findings, AI Recommendations, Trends, Screen Time) inline and togglable. iOS: Insights page mirrors the top-level structure but several key trends (Habit Streaks, Sleep Chart, Best Deep-Work Window, Mood & Energy, Sleep→Mood Correlation, Medication Adherence) are wrapped in collapsible DisclosureGroups via collapsibleCard helper, making them secondarily discoverable instead of always-visible.
divergences.androidBehavior: InsightsTab composes sections in a single Column with verticalScroll. Section visibility is driven by insightsSectionVisible() + selectedSections Set<String>. All content (except trends on certain gates) renders inline. Trends section always visible in the layout, with nested charts for Mood, Habit, Medication, Screen Time, Sleep, Journal—each auto-gated on data availability (e.g., habit trend only shows if trends.habitTrend.any { it.completedCount > 0 || it.missedCount > 0 }). Lines 196–457 of InsightsTab.kt show all sections rendered top-to-bottom with in-page filtering.
divergences.iosBehavior: InsightsView uses a ScrollView with VStack and inline rendering, BUT collapsibleCard helper (lines 229–249) wraps many trend cards in DisclosureGroup with collapsed state persisted via ChronosSettings.insightsCardCollapsed. Habit streaks (line 133), Sleep chart (line 138), Best deep-work window (line 143), Mood & energy (line 148), Sleep→mood correlation (line 152), Medication adherence (line 157) are all collapsible and default-collapsed. This hides valuable trend insights from first-glance, deviating from Android's eager-render-with-optional-filter approach.
divergences.fix: Remove collapsible wrappers from trend cards. Render them inline like Android: habitChart, sleepChart, moodChart, bestWindowCard, correlationCard, adherenceCard should always be visible (or gated only on data availability like Android, never on collapsed state). Remove the collapsibleCard helper usage for trends. Preserve the collapsible behavior only for the 'balance' card (day balance) if desired, as it mirrors Android's optional deep dive, but unfold findings and recommendations cards by default to match Android's eager rendering.

divergences.description: Android: The execution card shows a completion percentage with a visual progress bar, four metric stats (Planned/Actual/Missed/Drift with color-coded accents), a narrative + missed-block count, and an 'Open daily review' button triggering the end-of-day detailed review sheet. iOS: The execution metric card (periodSummaryCard) shows similar elements but the 'Day review' button is in the toolbar (top-right) instead of inside the card, and the narrative is inline without the detail-sheet affordance.
divergences.androidBehavior: InsightsTab execution section (lines 196–269): ChronosFilledTonalButton 'Open daily review' at line 258 calls onOpenFullReview, which launches the detailed DayReviewSheet showing planned-vs-actual breakdown per block. The card foregrounds the full-review action. onOpenFullReview callback is passed down from DayDialScreen.
divergences.iosBehavior: InsightsView execution summary (lines 264–308) shows metrics + narrative but has no 'Open daily review' button inline. Instead, RootView toolbar (line 170) has a Button('Day review') { showingDayReview = true }, which opens DayReviewSheet modally. The full-review action is topbar-owned, not card-owned.
divergences.fix: Add a button inside the execution-metric card (periodSummaryCard) that calls a callback to open the day-review sheet. Pass the callback down from the parent DayDialScreen. Change the toolbar button to be DayDialScreen-internal or remove the toolbar button entirely, keying the sheet open off the card button instead. This surfaces the detail-review action inline, matching Android's UX priority.

divergences.description: Android: The 'AI recommendations' section has a refresh button (with spinner during load) inline at line 388, next to the title. Recommendations are fed by InsightsRecommendationsPlanner (local heuristics) + optional GenAI. iOS: The recommendations card (line 424) has a refresh button at top-right, but it is NOT inside a DisclosureGroup—it is always expanded. However, the card structure and refresh UX differ: iOS button is smaller/styled differently, and recommendations are not wrapped in a collapsible.
divergences.androidBehavior: Lines 387–416 in InsightsTab.kt: Row with ChronosSectionTitle('AI recommendations') on the left, ChronosOutlinedButton with refresh icon + 'Refresh' label on the right (enabled only if !isRefreshing). Button shows a spinner while isRefreshing=true. RecommendationRow (lines 715–740) renders each recommendation with text, source label, and 'Apply' button.
divergences.iosBehavior: Lines 424–463 in InsightsView.swift: HStack with Label('AI recommendations') and a refresh button at trailing. The button is styled .bordered and disabled while isRefreshingRecommendations=true. RecommendationRow is absent; instead, recommendations are iterated via ForEach, each showing a lightbulb icon, text, source, but no explicit 'Apply' action—the recommendation is read-only.
divergences.fix: On iOS: Add an 'Apply' button to each recommendation row (mirroring Android's RecommendationRow). The callback should be wired up to the recommendation planner's apply logic. Ensure the refresh button styling and placement match Android more closely (same scale, same visual hierarchy).

divergences.description: Android: Review insights (severity-ranked findings) are always shown in a separate card with a list of ReviewInsightRow entries, each with a severity icon (Visibility/Analytics/Schedule), title, detail, type label, and optional GenAI source label. The list is sorted by severity (CRITICAL → WARNING → INFO) then type name. iOS: Findings are collapsible (wrapped in collapsibleCard, line 119) and rendered with similar icons + styling but the collapsible state defaults to collapsed, hiding findings from the initial view.
divergences.androidBehavior: Lines 336–354 in InsightsTab.kt: If insightsSectionVisible(InsightsSection.INSIGHTS), render orderedInsights (sorted by severity then type) in a ChronosListCard. ReviewInsightRow (lines 537–585) renders each with icon (Info/Warning/Critical mapped to Visibility/Analytics/Schedule), title, detail, severity label, and optional source. No collapsible wrapping.
divergences.iosBehavior: Lines 119–121 in InsightsView.swift: collapsibleCard(key: 'findings', title: 'Review findings') wraps findingsCard, which may be initially collapsed. findingRow (lines 392–404) has similar icon + styling but defaults hidden if the DisclosureGroup is folded.
divergences.fix: Remove the collapsibleCard wrapper from the findings card. Render findingsCard always expanded, mirroring Android's eager display. If user preference for collapsible state is desired, add a toggle elsewhere (e.g., in settings) but default to expanded.

divergences.description: Android: The category breakdown card shows the top category with a ★ star and concentration label, then lists all categories with progress bars, minutes, and percentage share. A concentration tip (suggesting context switching if focus is too high) is shown inline below the list. iOS: The concentration tip is missing; the category breakdown does not provide actionable guidance on focus variety.
divergences.androidBehavior: Lines 271–334 in InsightsTab.kt: categoryRows are iterated, the top row gets a ★ prefix and secondary color. focusConcentrationTip (lines 880–892) generates a tip based on share % and category count (e.g., 'Very high focus on X. Try splitting...'). Tip is shown at line 324 in the column.
divergences.iosBehavior: Lines 331–362 in InsightsView.swift: categoryBreakdownCard shows topCategory with ★ and concentration color, but no tip is calculated or displayed. The actionable guidance is absent.
divergences.fix: Implement focusConcentrationTip logic in iOS and render the tip text below the category rows, using the same thresholds as Android (share >= 0.85f for 'very high focus', >= 0.7f for 'most of day', etc.).

divergences.description: Android: The InsightsTrendSections component is a standalone, comprehensive trends section with day-balance insights, habit streaks, medication adherence, screen-time focus analysis (including distractions + nudges), journal history, evening reflection, sleep trends, and a sleep-log button. Each is a distinct ChronosListCard. iOS: The trends section is fragmented: habit streaks, sleep chart, best window, mood chart, and correlation card are separate collapsible sections (hidden by default). Sleep log entry has its own card at the bottom of the trends area. Journal and mood trends are less visually cohesive.
divergences.androidBehavior: InsightsTrendSections (InsightsTrendSections.kt, lines 52–477) composes all trends in a single Column with ChronosSpacing.Compact gaps. Each trend (mood, habit, medication, screen-time, journal, sleep) is gated on data availability but always rendered when data exists. The section is self-contained and placed at lines 445–457 in InsightsTab.kt.
divergences.iosBehavior: InsightsView trends (lines 131–162) are spread across multiple collapsibleCard helpers, each governing a single trend. The visual organization is scattered, and the user must expand each card to see the trend.
divergences.fix: Consolidate iOS trends into a single 'Trends' section (mirroring Android's structure). Render all trend charts and insights in a cohesive column, gated by data availability rather than collapsed state. If iPad layout requires restructuring, use a multi-column grid, but preserve the eager-render-on-data approach on iPhone.

divergences.description: Android: Screen time section is rendered as a single inline card (ScreenTimeCard, part of InsightsTrendSections). iOS: Screen time is rendered as a standalone ChronosGlassCard with a hourglass icon and informational message; it does not include real tracking data (as Screen Time data access requires DeviceActivity authorization on iOS).
divergences.androidBehavior: ScreenTimeCard (feature/daydial/src/main/java/com/ChronosFlow/VBCR/feature/daydial/ScreenTimeCard.kt) is composed at line 441 in InsightsTab.kt. The card displays focused vs. distracting app usage over the trend window (via trends.screenTimeTrend), focus percentage, goal tracking, best focus day, and distraction nudges.
divergences.iosBehavior: screenTimeCard (lines 552–565 in InsightsView.swift) is a placeholder: hourglass icon, 'Screen time' heading, and static message 'Track focused vs. distracting app time...'. No actual screen time data is shown.
divergences.fix: Integrate Screen Time framework (requires DeviceActivity + AppIntents authorization on iOS 15+) to fetch real screen time data on supported devices. Mirror Android's display: total focused %, focus goal tracking, best focus day, top distracting apps. If authorization is not granted, show the current placeholder. This aligns the iOS surface with Android's rich screen-time insights.

androidFlow: Android (DayDial-centric): Routines = "Templates" (TemplateBlueprint in-memory) accessed as a sidebar page (SidebarPage.TEMPLATES) within the DayDial screen. A routine exists both as a reusable in-day template (edited/applied within day context) and as a persisted Routine model. Access: (1) sidebar "Routines" tab → lists all templates + "Apply today/tomorrow/Seed day" actions + "Edit" + "Copy" + "Save current day as routine"; (2) right-side menu → onApplyTemplate (passes template ID to viewModel.applyRoutineToDate). No separate "Routines" destination. Apply uses ApplyRoutineToDateUseCase(routineId, date, startMinute) to instantiate all steps as TimeBlocks. Complete via CompleteRoutineForDateUseCase (marks routine.lastCompletedDate). Completion status derived from TimeBlocks carrying routineId + actualEndMinuteOfDay. Routines are NOT in the Quick-Add FAB menu (only new blocks/tasks/meds/habits/goals/journal/sleep).
iosFlow: iOS (tab-based): Routines = a standalone TabSection("Track") → "Routines" tab within RootView (ShellTab.routines). RoutinesView is a full-screen tab showing all routines as cards. Each card has: "Mark complete" (markComplete -> lastCompletedDate) + "Edit" + "Apply to day" (ApplyRoutineSheet). Apply opens a sheet with date/start-time pickers, previews instantiated blocks, calls apply() to insert TimeBlocks. Separate from Android's in-day template context entirely — routines never appear in DayDial, and there is no "save current day as routine" action. Routines are also NOT in the Quick-Add menu (QuickAdd.swift only lists block/task/med/habit/goal/journal/sleep). iOS instantiation logic mirrors Android exactly (ChronosCore.instantiateRoutine; uses floorDiv/floorMod).

divergences.description: Android routines = sidebar page within DayDial (accessed via SidebarPage.TEMPLATES in a modal sidebar). iOS routines = standalone tab in the main TabView.
divergences.androidBehavior: User opens DayDial → clicks sidebar → clicks "Routines" → sees templates inline within the DayDial context. Routines are a layer of the DayDial, not a separate destination.
divergences.iosBehavior: User taps the "Routines" tab in the main tab bar. Presents RoutinesView as its own full-screen tab (via ShellTab.routines).
divergences.fix: Remove ShellTab.routines from RootView's TabView. Move RoutinesView to be a sidebar page (new case in SidebarPage enum, e.g., SidebarPage.ROUTINES or reuse SidebarPage.TEMPLATES). Present RoutinesView as a sheet/navigation from DayDialScreen, not as a top-level tab. Update ios/ChronosFlow/App/RootView.swift: delete the Tab("Routines", ..., value: .routines) entry and the ShellTab.routines case. Create/reuse a RoutinesSheetTarget or extend DayDialScreen to navigate to routines within its sidebar context.

divergences.description: Android groups routines under 'morePages' with Journal, Reading List, Calendars, etc. (bottom of sidebar navigation). iOS places routines in 'Track' TabSection alongside Habits, Goals, Meds, Sleep, Journal.
divergences.androidBehavior: SidebarPage.TEMPLATES appears in .morePages list, accessed via a scrollable sidebar drill-down. Not a primary/root page like Tasks or Habits.
divergences.iosBehavior: Routines is a first-class tab in the Track section, peer to Habits/Goals/Meds/Sleep/Journal, which conflates 'long-lived tracking' with 'routine templates'. Android keeps routines in a distinct 'tools' tier.
divergences.fix: Move Routines out of TabSection("Track") in RootView. Either: (a) remove from TabView entirely and surface only via DayDial sidebar, or (b) create a new TabSection("Tools") or place under a different IA tier. If keeping it visible, place it below Review or alongside Settings, not in Track. Update ios/ChronosFlow/App/RootView.swift lines 104–108.

divergences.description: Android routines support in-day seeding ("Seed day" = ApplyRoutineToDateUseCase with anchor minute 0 to fill the current day with routine blocks) + save-current-day-as-routine action. iOS has only apply-to-date (with chosen start time) and no save-as-routine.
divergences.androidBehavior: SidebarPageContent.kt lines 501–535: three apply actions (Apply today, Apply tomorrow, Seed day) + button to save current day's plan as a new routine. The seeding instantly populates today with blocks at their default offsets. Routines act as both templates-in-context and saveable blueprints.
divergences.iosBehavior: RoutinesView + ApplyRoutineSheet: only date + start-time picker, then instantiate and save. No "seed day" (apply-with-anchor-0) + no "save this day" feature. Routines are immutable collections, not derived from the day's actual plan.
divergences.fix: (a) Add 'seed day' action to RoutineCard in ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Routines/RoutinesView.swift: insert a 4th button (alongside Edit, Mark complete, Apply to day) that applies the routine with start minute = 0, today, no sheet. (b) Add 'save current day as routine' button to DayDialScreen (where the day's blocks are available). This requires DayDialScreen to expose a callback (e.g., onSaveAsRoutine: (List<TimeBlock>) -> Void) that RoutinesView can receive. Instantiate a new Routine with the blocks' attributes and save to context. Mirror SidebarPageContent.kt lines 535 & appfunctions applyRoutine().

divergences.description: Android exposes routines as AI Assistant (AppFunction) targets: applyRoutine(routineName, dayOptional) is callable via natural-language commands. iOS has no AppFunction equivalent.
divergences.androidBehavior: ChronosAppFunctions.kt lines 808–829: @AppFunction suspend fun applyRoutine(...). Users can tell the AI "apply my morning routine tomorrow" and the system calls applyRoutineToDateUseCase. No iOS equivalent.
divergences.iosBehavior: No AppFunction metadata or AI-callable routine actions. Routines are UI-only; assistants cannot trigger them programmatically.
divergences.fix: Add a custom ShortCut intent to ios/ChronosFlow/AppIntents/ChronosAppIntents.swift that exposes 'Apply Routine' to Siri + Shortcuts. Define an intent that takes routine name + optional date, then calls the same instantiation logic. Mirror the Android AppFunction behavior (case-insensitive routine lookup, default to today, return success/failure).

divergences.description: Android's routine completion status (in sidebar) shows a completion summary ("X/Y blocks done") derived from TimeBlocks with routineId + actualEndMinuteOfDay. iOS shows lastCompletedDate in RoutineCard but no per-routine block completion tracking.
divergences.androidBehavior: SidebarPageContent.kt lines 485–492: deriveRoutineCompletions(blocks) groups all TimeBlocks by routineId and counts those with actualEndMinuteOfDay != null. Completion label shows "2/5 blocks done" inline.
divergences.iosBehavior: RoutineCard shows lastCompletedDate (e.g., "Completed today" or "Last completed X days ago"), not a count of completed blocks. No per-block tracking; only a binary "done today" state.
divergences.fix: Update RoutineCard in ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Routines/RoutinesView.swift to derive and display block completion like Android. Query TimeBlocks with routineId == routine.id for the viewed date (today), count those with actualEndMinuteOfDay != null, show "X/Y blocks done" label alongside lastCompletedDate. Requires passing the viewed date to RoutineCard (or having it read from an environment key @Environment(\.viewedDate)).

androidFlow:
Android accesses settings through the sidebar navigation model. Android has discrete sidebar pages (4 separate settings screens):
- AI_SETTINGS (privacy mode, preview model, auto-apply plan, planning style)
- PRIVACY_SYNC (app lock, sensitive content redaction, cloud sync, Wear link, companion app interop)
- NOTIFICATIONS (block/break reminders, meditation/habit/review reminders, quiet hours, sleep/journal reminder)
- APPEARANCE (theme mode, backdrop theme, dynamic color, glass, reduce motion, increase contrast)

All four are reachable via the sidebar navigation (feature/daydial/model/SidebarPage.kt) and accessed by routing to Day(target=TARGET_AI_SETTINGS/PRIVACY_SYNC/NOTIFICATIONS/APPEARANCE).

Feature flags (Habits, Medication, Goals, Journal, Sleep, Review, AI Advisor) are controlled in the Developer panel within the sidebar (implemented in SidebarPageContent.kt as a developer section listing 7 toggles).

Onboarding flow (app/.../onboarding/ChronosOnboarding.kt) is 3 paged screens: intro → feature selector → permissions priming. Feature selection persists to the same flags used in the day-targets. After onboarding, the user can reach settings via the sidebar navigation or command palette/FAB menu.
iosFlow:
iOS accesses settings as a single monolithic tab in the TabView shell (RootView.swift). All settings (appearance, AI, notifications, privacy, feature flags) are on one SettingsView (Settings/SettingsView.swift) using a grouped Form with multiple sections in order: Appearance → AI & Planning → Notifications → Privacy & Sync → Connected Apps (Meridian) → Screen Time → Features → Data → About.

There is no sidebar or multi-page navigation — all settings sections are within one scrollable form. Feature flags appear in a single "Features" section listing 7 toggles (identical list to Android).

Onboarding (ios/.../Features/Onboarding/OnboardingView.swift) is a 6-page TabView: 4 info pages → feature selector → permissions priming. Feature selection binds directly to ChronosSettings.shared and persists immediately via UserDefaults, same as Android.

Both Android and iOS use feature graduation (promotion markers) to ensure off-by-default features ship on by default without stranding old installs with stale false values.

divergences.description: Android has discrete sidebar pages for settings (4 screens: AI Settings, Privacy & Sync, Notifications, Appearance), accessed via targeted deep links. iOS has all settings in a single monolithic scrollable Form view with no multi-page navigation.
divergences.androidBehavior: User taps sidebar, selects settings section (AI_SETTINGS/PRIVACY_SYNC/NOTIFICATIONS/APPEARANCE), routes to Day(target=...) which renders SidebarPageContent for that page
divergences.iosBehavior: User taps Settings tab in TabView, sees one SettingsView with 9 grouped sections stacked in a Form
divergences.fix: Break iOS SettingsView.swift into separate views per section. Create a navigation stack within the Settings tab that routes to sub-pages: SettingsAppearanceView, SettingsAIView, SettingsNotificationsView, SettingsPrivacySyncView (with collapsible groups). Use NavigationLink or NavigationStack to mirror Android's sidebar page model. This requires refactoring ios/ChronosFlow/Settings/SettingsView.swift to use NavigationStack and creating 4 new view files.

divergences.description: Android groups settings into 4 logical pages (each is a full screen); iOS piles them all into one vertically scrollable Form. The cognitive load and scroll distance are fundamentally different.
divergences.androidBehavior: Each settings category (AI, Privacy/Sync, Notifications, Appearance) is its own full-screen section in the sidebar, with its own header, collapsible groups where needed, and dedicated real estate.
divergences.iosBehavior: All settings stack in one Form: 9 sections scroll past each other vertically. No spatial separation, no navigation breadcrumbs.
divergences.fix: Reorganize iOS to present settings as a tiered navigation: top-level Settings tab shows a list of 4 settings pages (Appearance, AI & planning, Notifications, Privacy & Sync) with their icons and descriptions, each as a NavigationLink. Create 4 separate view files (SettingsAppearanceView.swift, SettingsAIView.swift, SettingsNotificationsView.swift, SettingsPrivacySyncView.swift) that each render their section as a Form. This matches Android's 4-page model.

divergences.description: Android has collapsible sections in Privacy & Sync and Notifications (with persisted expand-state keys like privacy.appPermissions.expanded). iOS has some DisclosureGroups (sensitive content, cloud sync, wear link, companion app) but NOT in Notifications or the top-level Appearance settings.
divergences.androidBehavior: Notifications page has always-visible toggles; Privacy & Sync has 5 collapsible sections (App lock always visible, then Sensitive content / Cloud sync / Wear link / Companion app as DisclosureGroups with expand state persisted in DataStore).
divergences.iosBehavior: Notifications has all toggles always visible; Privacy & Sync has DisclosureGroups for Sensitive content / Cloud sync / Wear link / Connected apps, but misses the explicit 'App Permissions' collapsible that Android shows.
divergences.fix: In SettingsPrivacySyncView, add a DisclosureGroup for 'App Permissions' (always-visible on Android but still collapsible on iOS) that wraps the medication lock + HealthKit sleep toggles. Persist its expanded state via ChronosSettings just like the others (add privacyAppPermissionsExpanded to ChronosSettings if missing, which ios/ChronosFlow/Settings/ChronosSettings.swift already has at line 85). Wrap in DisclosureGroup(isExpanded: $settings.privacyAppPermissionsExpanded) { Toggle(...) }.

divergences.description: Android separates settings into 4 full-screen sidebars, each with its own visual hierarchy and header. iOS shows 9 sections in one scrollable Form, with the same importance/visual weight. No breadcrumb or 'back' affordance on iOS.
divergences.androidBehavior: Each sidebar page (AI_SETTINGS, PRIVACY_SYNC, etc.) renders as a full screen with a header saying 'AI Settings' / 'Privacy & Sync' / etc., then collapsible groups and controls below. User can back out via the sidebar.
divergences.iosBehavior: SettingsView is one Form with section headers ('Appearance', 'AI & planning', 'Notifications', etc.) but no affordance to navigate between them or collapse the entire section — everything is in one scroll view.
divergences.fix: Replace the single-Form SettingsView with a NavigationStack that shows a list view of 4 settings category tiles (each with an icon and label, matching the Android sidebar icons). Tapping a tile routes to its dedicated view. Add a back button or use NavigationStack's automatic back affordance. This gives iOS the same visual/navigation separation as Android.

divergences.description: Android onboarding has 3 pages (intro, feature selector, permissions). iOS onboarding has 6 pages (4 info pages, feature selector, permissions). The total page count and flow is different.
divergences.androidBehavior: 3-page HorizontalPager: Page 0 = dial intro, Page 1 = feature selector, Page 2 = permissions. User sees 3 dots, can skip early, gets 'Next' button advancing pages sequentially.
divergences.iosBehavior: 6-page TabView: Pages 0–3 are info pages ('Your day as a dial', 'Plan and protect time', 'Learn and improve', 'Stay on track'), Page 4 = feature selector, Page 5 = permissions. More intro, but identical feature/permission logic.
divergences.fix: Consolidate iOS onboarding to 3 pages: merge the 4 info pages into a single pager that cycles through them (maybe show 1 per tab, or keep 4 but acknowledge that Android shows only 1 intro). Alternatively, add a 4th page to Android to match iOS's 'Plan and protect' and 'Learn and improve' messages (but the brief says do not modify Android). Keep iOS as-is: it's a superset UX, not a divergence in *function*. No fix needed here unless you want parity down to page count.

divergences.description: Android Notifications settings has 'Sleep & Journal log reminder' (logReminderEnabled). iOS has the same toggle, but the naming is slightly different: iOS calls it 'Evening log reminder (20:00)' while Android context suggests it's bound to the sleep/journal flow. Both are present and functional.
divergences.androidBehavior: onSleepJournalLogReminderChanged callback in SidebarPageContent; label is 'Sleep & journal log reminder'.
divergences.iosBehavior: Toggle("Evening log reminder (20:00)", isOn: $settings.logReminderEnabled) in notificationsSection. Exact same underlying flag (logReminderEnabled in ChronosSettings, notif.logReminder in UserDefaults).
divergences.fix: No critical fix needed. Both are synced. If you want exact label parity, rename iOS's toggle from 'Evening log reminder (20:00)' to 'Log sleep & journal reminder' to match Android's grouping with the sleep/journal features.

divergences.description: Android has explicit 'Protect focus blocks' / 'Add breaks automatically' / 'Preserve manual blocks' toggles in AI_SETTINGS under Planning. iOS does not expose these in the AI & planning section — they are missing entirely.
divergences.androidBehavior: SidebarPageContent.kt lines 961–963: CheckboxSetting for 'Protect focus blocks', 'Add breaks automatically', 'Preserve manual blocks', each with callbacks onProtectFocusChanged, onAddBreaksAutomaticallyChanged, onPreserveManualBlocksChanged.
divergences.iosBehavior: SettingsView has only aiEnabled, planningStyle, and autoApplyPlan toggles. No toggles for focus protection or auto-break insertion.
divergences.fix: Add 3 new properties to ChronosSettings (ios/ChronosFlow/Settings/ChronosSettings.swift): protectFocusBlocks, addBreaksAutomatically, preserveManualBlocks, each with UserDefaults persistence (e.g., planningStyle.protectFocus, planningStyle.autoBreaks, planningStyle.preserveManual). Then add 3 Toggle rows to SettingsAIView under the Planning style picker, bound to these properties. Wire up the iOS app to respect these flags in the planner (requires coordination with the ML model layer to read the flags on plan generation).

area: Calendar import, sync, and interop (DevTime integration)
androidFlow: Android implements calendar via multiple layers: (1) DayDialScreen shows calendar-permission flow with rationale dialogs, foreground-sync, and export-to-calendar actions on individual blocks. (2) SidebarPage.CALENDARS provides a dedicated calendar management page with month picker, sync status, permission flows, and a detailed-calendar section that filters imported events by preset (All/Schedule/Calendar) and per-source checkboxes. (3) Calendar overlay on dial shows device events as ghost arcs. (4) InteropSync handles DevTime peer-sync as a background worker with 6h cadence, mirroring tasks deterministically and scheduling reminders. Surfaces in Settings > Connected apps section.
iosFlow: iOS has minimal, fragmented calendar surface: (1) DayDialScreen toggles a calendar overlay (hidden in plan menu) that draws readonly event arcs via CalendarOverlayProvider/EventKit. (2) Calendar permissions are silently requested in background. (3) No dedicated calendar management page. (4) SettingsView has no calendar section. (5) InteropSync works but surfaces no UI: no sync timestamp, no failure message, no Connected apps card, no consent toggle. (6) No calendar ring presets, no per-source filters, no Calendar-only mode.

divergences.description: Android has SidebarPage.CALENDARS dedicated full page with month picker, sync status, permission flows, and detailed calendar list. iOS has no calendar management page; overlay is hidden in a menu.
divergences.androidBehavior: User navigates to Settings > More (sidebar) > Calendars page, sees calendar month picker, sync status banner, connection summary, and Detailed Calendar section with event timeline.
divergences.iosBehavior: User navigates to Plan tab, opens menu (wand icon), finds Show/Hide calendar overlay toggle buried in a list with AI plan, fill gaps, fix schedule, and repair with AI options. No dedicated calendar page.
divergences.fix: Create ios/ChronosFlow/Features/Calendar/CalendarManagementView.swift as a new SettingsView section. Mirror the Android Calendars sidebar page structure with: (1) MonthPicker for date navigation (2) CalendarSyncStatusCard showing connection state and last-sync timestamp (3) Detailed timeline list of imported events with per-source filtering via segmented buttons (All/Schedule/Calendar) and a filter menu for per-source checkboxes. Add to SettingsView.swift as a new NavigationLink or DisclosureGroup in privacySyncSection.

divergences.description: Android consolidates calendar UI in SidebarPageContent (dedicated page) and DayDialScreen (permissions/export). iOS scatters calendar across DayDialScreen overlay toggle, CalendarOverlay.swift provider, and no SettingsView section.
divergences.androidBehavior: Calendar management in one sidebar page (SidebarPage.CALENDARS). Export/import via PendingCalendarAction enums. Permission flow unified in DayDialCalendarPermissions.kt.
divergences.iosBehavior: Calendar overlay in DayDialScreen. Interop sync runs in background with no UI. Permission requests implicit. No permission-rationale dialog.
divergences.fix: Consolidate iOS surfaces into CalendarManagementView + CalendarPermissionsHandler. Move overlay toggle from plan menu to CalendarManagementView. Expose interop sync status (last sync, result, consent toggle) in new ConnectedAppsView within privacySyncSection. Add calendar-permissions dialog in SettingsView mirroring Android's rationale + resolution logic.

divergences.description: Android shows calendar events in detailed-calendar section with preset filters (All 6 sources, Schedule 4, Calendar 2) and per-source toggles. iOS shows no calendar event list.
divergences.androidBehavior: SidebarPageContent.kt lines 750-905: Three segmented-button presets map to CalendarTimelinePreset enum. Filter menu shows Hide Completed, Connected Calendar Only, and per-source checkboxes. List renders SidebarTimelineItems grouped by source.
divergences.iosBehavior: DayDialScreen only shows overlay events as ghost arcs. No event list, filtering, or per-source visibility controls.
divergences.fix: In CalendarManagementView, add timeline section mirroring Android's Detailed Calendar. Import CalendarTimelinePreset enum and filter logic (SidebarPageContent.kt lines 1533-1557). Render segmented buttons for All/Schedule/Calendar. Add filter menu with Hide Completed toggle and per-source checkboxes. Query imported TimeBlock and quick-item records for selected date and render grouped by source label.

divergences.description: Android renders calendar events inline in sidebar with detail cards showing source label, time, category, and quick-action buttons. iOS shows no calendar event list UI.
divergences.androidBehavior: Lines 750-905 in SidebarPageContent.kt render scrollable list of SidebarTimelineItems with title, source label, time, category detail, status, and optional action buttons. Events grouped by source with section headers showing count.
divergences.iosBehavior: No timeline list for calendar events.
divergences.fix: Create CalendarTimelineView mirroring Android's SidebarTimelineItem rendering. Display filtered events as scrollable list with Section headers for source labels with counts. Render rows with title, time, category/detail, and status. For quick items include action buttons (Complete, Take, Missed).

divergences.description: Android exposes calendar permissions flow (READ and WRITE) with rationale dialogs, permission check on app resume, and actionable error states in sidebar. iOS silently requests EventKit access; no user-facing flow or status.
divergences.androidBehavior: DayDialCalendarPermissions.kt defines CalendarPermissionStatus (readGranted, writeGranted, permanentlyDenied, shouldShowRationale), PendingCalendarAction enum, and resolution logic. DayDialScreen.kt has calendarPermissionLauncher/state. SidebarPageContent.kt lines 637-744 render collapsible Calendar Sync section with status and actionable buttons.
divergences.iosBehavior: CalendarOverlayProvider.requestAccess() silently requests in background. No rationale dialog, permission state UI, or error messages.
divergences.fix: Add calendar-permission handling to CalendarManagementView and SettingsView. Port CalendarPermissionStatus and PendingCalendarAction patterns from Android. Add requestCalendarAccess() with a dialog (like HealthKitSleepImporter.swift). Render permission status card in CalendarManagementView showing current state (all granted / read-only / denied), actionable buttons (Request, Open Settings, Enable Write), and status messages matching Android's copy.

divergences.description: Android surfaces interop peer sync (DevTime import) prominently in Settings > Connected apps with last-sync timestamp, result message, and consent toggle. iOS has working InteropSync but zero UI.
divergences.androidBehavior: InteropSyncManager.kt and InteropContract.kt define sync pipeline. SidebarPageContent.kt lines 1068-1076 render CompanionAppStatusCard with sync status and Connected Apps section.
divergences.iosBehavior: InteropSync.swift implements full pipeline. InteropSync.lastSyncDate and lastResult stored in App-Group defaults but never displayed. No consent toggle.
divergences.fix: Create ConnectedAppsView in SettingsView showing interop status. Add to privacySyncSection as new DisclosureGroup (like wearLinkGroup). Render: (1) Last sync timestamp via InteropSync.lastSyncDate using formatLastSyncedLabel, (2) Last result message (InteropSync.lastResult), (3) Sync Now button, (4) Consent toggle bound to ChronosSettings.interopConsentGranted. Add ChronosSettings.interopConsentGranted boolean (default false) that gates InteropSync.runSync().

divergences.description: Android surfaces block-level calendar export actions (ExportBlock, RefreshBlock, RemoveBlock) in sidebar's Detailed Calendar section. iOS has no such UI.
divergences.androidBehavior: PendingCalendarAction enum includes ExportBlock(blockId), RefreshBlock(blockId), RemoveBlock(blockId). These map to viewModel methods. Action buttons in sidebar timeline rows trigger these.
divergences.iosBehavior: TimeBlockEditorSheet has no export-to-calendar button or action.
divergences.fix: Add Calendar Export field to TimeBlockEditorSheet. Show linked-calendar-event indicator when block.externalCalendarEventID != nil. Add buttons to Refresh, Remove, or (if not linked) Export to Calendar. Wire to viewModel methods matching Android's exportBlockToCalendar/refreshCalendarExport/removeCalendarExport semantics.
